items.title: Algebraic cycles and the cycle group of a scheme of finite type over a field
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$
([[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]], [[def-scheme-over-base]]).
An **algebraic cycle** on $X$ is a formal $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of
integral closed subschemes of $X$ ([[def-integral-scheme]],
[[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]); it is **finite** when the combination is
finite. For an integer $d$, the **group of $d$-cycles** is the free abelian
group

$$Z_d(X):=\bigoplus_{V} \mathbb Z\cdot[V],$$

Here the dimension of any scheme is the supremum of lengths of strict chains
of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of its underlying space, with
$\dim\varnothing=-\infty$. This extends the Noetherian convention
[[def-dimension-noetherian-topological-space]] without requiring
quasi-compactness. The direct sum runs over the integral closed subschemes $V\subseteq X$ of
dimension $d$ ([[def-dimension-noetherian-topological-space]],
[[def-noetherian-topological-space]], [[def-free-abelian-group]]); for finite type $X$ one writes
$Z_*(X)=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}Z_d(X)$. The **support** $|\alpha|$ of a cycle
$\alpha=\sum_i n_i[V_i]$ is the union of the $V_i$ with $n_i\ne0$, a closed
subset of $X$; a cycle is **effective** if all $n_i\ge0$.

**Conventions.** (i) A cycle class may be represented by a locally finite sum
in the situations below; finite sums suffice for the schemes of finite type
over a field used in this pair. (ii) All integral closed subschemes are taken
with the reduced structure, and $[V]$ denotes the associated basis element;
the fundamental cycle of an integral $X$ of dimension $n$ is $[X]\in Z_n(X)$.
(iii) For $X$ equidimensional of pure dimension $n$ one writes
$A^p(X):=A_{n-p}(X)$ for the codimension-$p$ Chow group once $A_*$ is
available (def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence). (iv) No choice
is used in this definition beyond the free abelian group on the set of
subvarieties ([[def-free-abelian-group]]). For a locally finite type scheme
not assumed quasi-compact, the locally finite cycle group consists instead of
formal sums whose component supports meet each quasi-compact open in only
finitely many terms. Its restriction to every such open is a finite cycle. The
displayed free direct sum is the finite-cycle group; throughout assertions on
merely locally finite type schemes use the locally finite group. For finite
type schemes the two groups coincide. For general locally finite type $X$,
$Z_*(X)$ denotes locally finite sums over all dimensions; it need not be the
direct sum of the $Z_d(X)$ when component dimensions are unbounded. Every
fixed-dimensional operation below is defined degreewise.
items.strategy:
Definition. The only points requiring care are: the free abelian group on the set of integral closed subschemes of $X$ of dimension $d$ exists ([[def-free-abelian-group]]); the set is well defined because dimension is a property of the underlying topological space ([[def-dimension-noetherian-topological-space]]); and the support of a finite combination is closed. Compare Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 1.1-1.3 and Stacks 42.8 (tag 02QY ff.), whose ``cycles with support'' convention is a mild generalization; we use the classical finite-support version of Fulton, which is what the later constructions in this pair use.

items.title: The order function of a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), used through the
finite-length suppliers in (1) and the regular-local-to-DVR supplier in (4). Let $A$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian
local domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and fraction field
$K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ ([[def-local-ring]], [[def-noetherian-ring]],
[[def-krull-dimension-of-a-ring]], [[def-field-of-fractions]]). For a nonzero
$A$-module $M$ of finite length write $\ell_A(M)$ for its length
([[def-composition-series-and-length-of-a-module]]). For $0\ne r\in K$ choose
$a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$ with $r=a/b$ and set
$$\operatorname{ord}_A(r):=\ell_A(A/aA)-\ell_A(A/bA)\in\mathbb Z.$$
Then:

1. $A/aA$ and $A/bA$ have finite length, so $\operatorname{ord}_A(r)$ is
   defined. For either nonzero element $x=a$ or $b$, if $x$ is a unit then
   $A/xA=0$ has length $0$; otherwise $A/xA$ is Noetherian and its unique
   prime is $\mathfrak m/xA$, so it has dimension $0$ and, by the
   Noetherian dimension-zero finite-length theorem (using AC), finite length.
2. The value $\operatorname{ord}_A(r)$ does not depend on the presentation
   $r=a/b$: if $a/b=c/d$ with $a,b,c,d\ne0$, then $ad=bc$, and the two exact
   sequences $0\to A/aA\xrightarrow{\,d\,}A/adA\to A/dA\to0$ and
   $0\to A/cA\xrightarrow{\,b\,}A/bcA\to A/bA\to0$, together with additivity
   of length in short exact sequences
   ([[cor-length-is-additive-in-short-exact-sequences]]), give
   $\ell(A/aA)-\ell(A/bA)=\ell(A/cA)-\ell(A/dA)$.
3. $\operatorname{ord}_A(rs)=\operatorname{ord}_A(r)+\operatorname{ord}_A(s)$
   and $\operatorname{ord}_A(r^{-1})=-\operatorname{ord}_A(r)$ for
   $r,s\in K^*$; $\operatorname{ord}_A(r)=0$ for $r\in A^*$;
   $\operatorname{ord}_A(r)\ge0$ for $r\in A\setminus\{0\}$, with equality if and only if
   $r\in A^*$.
4. If $A$ is a discrete valuation ring with normalized valuation $v_A$
   ([[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]), then $\operatorname{ord}_A=v_A$; if $A$
   is regular of dimension one, $\operatorname{ord}_A$ is the normalized
   valuation of the discrete valuation ring $A$
   ([[thm-equivalent-characterisations-of-a-dvr]]).
items.strategy:
Elementary. Finiteness of the lengths in (1): $A/aA$ is a Noetherian ring of dimension $0$, hence Artinian, hence of finite length. Claim (2) is the two exact-sequence computation displayed in the statement, using additivity of length ([[cor-length-is-additive-in-short-exact-sequences]]); the maps are injective because $A$ is a domain and $b,d\ne0$. Claim (3) follows by inserting finitely many intermediate terms and using the exact sequence $0\to A/bA\xrightarrow{a}A/abA\to A/aA\to0$, which gives $\ell(A/abA)=\ell(A/aA)+\ell(A/bA)$; the sign and positivity statements follow from $\ell=0\iff$ the quotient vanishes. Claim (4) is immediate from the definitions of length and of the normalized valuation. This is the order function used in Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, A.3 and proved there for arbitrary one-dimensional Noetherian local rings via Herbrand quotients; Stacks 42.2-42.6 (Key Lemma, tag 0EAX) proves the general form. The present lemma is the special case needed to define the divisor of a rational function on an integral closed subscheme (def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence).

items.title: Grothendieck groups of coherent sheaves and of vector bundles on a scheme
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
coherent-category and higher-direct-image suppliers. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme
([[def-locally-noetherian-and-noetherian-scheme]]). Then the category of
coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules is abelian
([[thm-coherent-sheaves-abelian-noetherian-scheme]],
[[def-coherent-module-scheme]]), and the category of finite locally free
$\mathcal O_X$-modules of locally constant rank is an exact category
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]).

1. The **Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves** $K_0(X):=K_0(\operatorname{Coh}(X))$
   is the abelian group with one generator $[\mathcal F]$ for each isomorphism class of coherent
   sheaves, subject to $[\mathcal F]=[\mathcal F']+[\mathcal F'']$ for every
   short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$
   ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]]);
   existence of the group is the group completion of the commutative monoid
   modulo the exact-sequence relations. These isomorphism classes form a set:
   on a fixed set-indexed affine cover, finite presentations give a set of
   local module models, and their overlap isomorphisms form sets; gluing
   those data gives a set of representatives. The same applies to vector
   bundles, using finite free local models.
2. The **Grothendieck group of vector bundles** $K^0(X)$ is the abelian group
   with one generator $[\mathcal E]$ for each isomorphism class of finite locally free sheaves of
   locally constant rank, subject to $[\mathcal E]=[\mathcal E']+[\mathcal E'']$
   for every exact sequence $0\to\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E''\to0$
   of such sheaves. Tensor product makes $K^0(X)$ a commutative ring with unit
   $[\mathcal O_X]$ ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]],
   [[lem-tensor-qc-modules-quasi-coherent]]), and makes $K_0(X)$ a
   $K^0(X)$-module via $[\mathcal E]\cdot[\mathcal F]:=[\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal F]$,
   using that tensoring with a locally free sheaf is exact.
3. Every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of locally Noetherian schemes induces
   $f^*:K^0(Y)\to K^0(X)$ by pullback of locally free sheaves
   ([[lem-pullback-qc-module-quasi-coherent]],
   [[lem-dual-locally-free-and-base-change]]); flat $f$ also induces
   $f^*:K_0(Y)\to K_0(X)$.
4. Under the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
   coherent-cohomology suppliers, if $f:X\to Y$ is proper between finite type
   schemes over a field, the higher direct images $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ are
   coherent ([[thm-proper-pushforward-coherent]]) and vanish for $q\gg0$ over
   affine opens of $Y$ ([[thm-cohomological-dimension-noetherian-scheme]],
   with the global bound $q>\dim X$); the resulting pushforward
   $f_!:K_0(X)\to K_0(Y)$ is defined in def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory.
5. The natural map $K^0(X)\to K_0(X)$, $[\mathcal E]\mapsto[\mathcal E]$, is
   well defined and additive; under the same Axiom of Choice premise it is an
   isomorphism when $X$ is a regular quasi-projective scheme of finite type
   over a field (lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves).
items.strategy: Definitions together with the standard exactness properties. For (3), pullback of a locally free sheaf is locally free and pullback preserves exact sequences of locally free sheaves ([[lem-pullback-qc-module-quasi-coherent]]), so $f^*$ is defined; for flat $f$, pullback of a short exact sequence of coherent sheaves is exact ($-\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal O_X$ is exact when $\mathcal O_X$ is flat over $\mathcal O_Y$), so $f^*$ is defined on $K_0$. For (2), tensoring a short exact sequence of coherent sheaves with a locally free sheaf is exact, so the $K^0$-action is well defined; the ring axioms are those of the tensor product. Reference: Stacks 42.69 (Appendix B: rational equivalence and $K$-groups, tag 0AYD) and Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 4-5 (the Grothendieck groups of coherent and locally free sheaves and their ring structure), and Vakil 245 Class 18 Section 2.2 (definitions of $K_0X$ and $K^0X$, functoriality, module structure, projection formula).

items.title: Smooth immersions have regular equations, normal exact sequences and smooth deformation charts
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
regular-local and smooth differential suppliers. For a closed immersion
$i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ of smooth finite type schemes over a field, with pure
dimensions $n,m$ and constant codimension $d=m-n$, the ideal is locally
generated by a regular sequence of length $d$, $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is
locally free of rank $d$, and
$$0\to\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2\to i^*\Omega^1_{Y/k}\to\Omega^1_{X/k}\to0$$
is exact. Its dual gives $0\to T_X\to i^*T_Y\to N_{X/Y}\to0$. Locally in the
étale topology the embedding is the inverse image of the coordinate inclusion
$\mathbb A^n\subset\mathbb A^m$. Consequently
$\operatorname{Bl}_{X\times\{\infty\}}(Y\times\mathbb P^1)$ is smooth; if $Y$
is quasi-projective, this blowup is quasi-projective. The same immersion and
normal assertions hold on locally closed presentations, by restriction. More
generally, a section $s:T\to P$ of a smooth morphism of locally Noetherian
schemes of constant relative dimension $r$ is a regular immersion of
codimension $r$. Its regular equations and normal bundle commute with every
base change on $T$, including singular bases.
items.strategy:
At a point $x\in X$ the ambient regular local ring $R=\mathcal O_{Y,x}$ and its regular quotient $S=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ have the same residue field. The local dimension/transcendence supplier gives $\dim R-\dim S=m-n=d$. The regular-quotient parameter supplier generates the ideal by $d$ members of a regular parameter system. Finite generation permits shrinking until those germs generate the ideal as functions. The first positive Koszul homology vanishes, so a relation among their conormal classes has every coefficient in the ideal; they are a basis of $I/I^2$. In the right-exact conormal sequence, the surjection from the free rank-$m$ differentials to the free rank-$n$ differentials splits locally. Its kernel is free rank $d$. The surjection from the free rank-$d$ conormal module to this kernel is an isomorphism by the determinant criterion over the local ring. This proves left exactness, and dualizing this locally split vector-bundle sequence gives the tangent sequence, without asserting a global splitting.
Choose functions on $X$ whose differentials give an étale coordinate basis near $x$, as provided by the smooth Jacobian supplier, and lift them to $Y$; append the $d$ ideal generators. Their differentials form a basis of $\Omega^1_{Y/k}$ near $x$ by the conormal sequence. The resulting morphism $Y\to\mathbb A^m$ is étale after shrinking by the Jacobian criterion, and its inverse image of the coordinate $\mathbb A^n$ is exactly $X$, since its first $d$ functions generate the ideal. Flat base change commutes with the blowup. The blowup of $\mathbb A^m\times\mathbb A^1_t$ along $(a_1,\ldots,a_d,t)$ has $t$-chart coordinates $(a_1/t,\ldots,a_d/t,t)$ and the untouched $n$ coordinates; its $a_j$-charts have coordinates $(a_j,a_l/a_j\ (l\ne j),t/a_j)$ and the untouched coordinates. Each chart is an affine space of dimension $m+1$, and the original blowup charts are their étale base changes. Away from infinity the family is the product with the smooth curve. Thus the entire deformation blowup is smooth. If $Y$ is quasi-projective, a projective morphism from its blowup gives a quasi-projective total space: realize the coherent Rees ideal after an ample twist by finitely many generators, embed its blowup into a projective bundle over $Y\times\mathbb P^1$, and compose the quasi-projective immersions. This uses the ample generation and blowup projectivity suppliers; additivity of the tangent class uses only the exact sequence. This is the arbitrary-smooth-ambient extension of the published projective-space calculation, not an application of that narrower statement outside its hypotheses. For the relative section assertion, use [[thm-smooth-local-standard-form]] to factor a neighbourhood of $s(t)$ étale over $\mathbb A^r_T$. Compose $s$ with its $r$ coordinates and subtract their values on the section. The equations $x_i-s^*x_i$ form a polynomial regular sequence on $\mathbb A^r_T$, even when $T$ is singular, by successive evaluation of monic coordinate equations. Their pullbacks remain regular under the flat étale map. The resulting inverse image of the coordinate graph is étale over $T$ and has the given section. That section is an open immersion: in a standard étale chart $(A[z]/P)_g$, the section sends $z$ to $a\in A$, with $P(a)=0$ and $P'(a)$ a unit after shrinking the base. Factor $P(z)=(z-a)Q(z)$, where $Q(a)=P'(a)$. On the open $D(Q)$ the relation is $z=a$, so that chart of the section is isomorphic to its base. Thus, after shrinking the ambient neighbourhood, the coordinate-zero inverse image equals the image of $s$ with its scheme structure. This proves regularity and codimension $r$. The polynomial sequence remains regular after arbitrary base change, and the étale map remains flat, proving the same assertion after every base change and the normal-bundle identification. This supplies the arbitrary singular-base section fact needed for the Gysin unit and operational-ring inverse, rather than importing it from a smooth absolute-ambient lemma.

items.title: Rational equivalence and the Chow group of cycles
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the order
function of [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]]; it is used
there for the finiteness of the lengths, and here only through that order
function. Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type
over $k$. For $d\in\mathbb Z$ let $\operatorname{Rat}_d(X)\subseteq Z_d(X)$ be
the subgroup generated by all cycles of the form
$$(i_W)_*\operatorname{div}(r),\qquad \operatorname{div}(r)=\sum_{V\subseteq W}\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{W,V}}(r)\,[V],$$
where $W\subseteq X$ is an integral closed subscheme of dimension $d+1$
([[def-integral-scheme]]), $i_W:W\hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion,
$r\in k(W)^*$ is a nonzero rational function on $W$
([[def-sheaf-total-quotient-rings]], [[def-field-of-fractions]]), the sum runs
over the integral closed subschemes $V\subseteq W$ of dimension $d$, and
$\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{W,V}}(r)$ is the order function of
[[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]] for the one-dimensional
Noetherian local domain $\mathcal O_{W,V}$ ([[def-local-ring]]). The sum is
locally finite, and finite when $W$ is of finite type, as proved below. The
elements of $\operatorname{Rat}_d(X)$ are the $d$-cycles **rationally
equivalent to zero**; two cycles are **rationally equivalent** if their
difference is, written $\alpha\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}\beta$. The **Chow group of
$d$-cycles** is
$$A_d(X):=Z_d(X)/\operatorname{Rat}_d(X),\qquad A_*(X)=\bigoplus_{d}A_d(X)\quad\text{for finite type }X.$$

**Basic facts.** (i) Rational equivalence is an equivalence relation compatible
with the group structure, by definition. (ii) If $W$ is a *normal* integral
closed subscheme, then $\operatorname{div}(r)$ agrees with the principal Weil
divisor of $r$ computed with the divisor theory of
[[def-order-codimension-one-rational-function]],
[[def-principal-weil-divisor-and-class-group]]; in particular for $X$ integral
of dimension $n$ and normal (e.g. smooth), $A_n(X)\cong\mathbb Z$ generated by
$[X]$ and $A_d(X)=0$ for $d>\dim X$. (iii) For $X$ equidimensional of pure
dimension $n$, set $A^p(X):=A_{n-p}(X)$; this is the codimension grading used
throughout. (iv) Equivalent presentation: $\alpha\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}0$ if and
only if $\alpha=\sum_i (i_{W_i})_*\operatorname{div}(r_i)$ as above; this is the
"Fulton 1.6" definition with supports on closed subschemes of
$X\times\mathbb P^1$ specialized, and it is Stacks' Definition 42.19.1 (tag
02RW). For merely locally finite type $X$, use the locally finite cycle group of
[[def-algebraic-cycle-and-cycle-group]] and locally finite sums of principal
divisors supported on locally finite families of the subvarieties $W$. These
sums define the rational-equivalence subgroup; finite generation as written
above applies when $X$ is of finite type. In the general case the total group
$A_*(X)$ is the quotient of the total locally finite cycle group by locally
finite sums of these relations, allowing unbounded dimensions as in
[[def-algebraic-cycle-and-cycle-group]]. Thus pullback along a non-quasi-compact
flat map uses locally finite cycles, not a finite-support sum with infinitely
many components.

**Well-definedness of the divisor sum.** Let $W$ be integral of dimension $d+1$
and $0\ne r\in k(W)^*$. On an affine open chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq W$
with $W$ of finite type over $k$, write $r=a/b$ with $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$
under the identification $k(W)=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. For an integral closed
subscheme $V\subseteq W$ of dimension $d$ meeting the chart in a height-one
prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, the order $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{W,V}}(r)$
of [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]] vanishes unless
$\mathfrak p$ contains $a$ or $b$, hence unless $\mathfrak p$ contains $ab$; then
$\mathfrak p$ is minimal over the principal ideal $(ab)$, hence has height one
by [[cor-minimal-prime-over-a-nonzerodivisor-has-height-one]]. A Noetherian ring
has only finitely many minimal primes over the radical of a principal ideal
([[cor-radical-ideal-has-finitely-many-minimal-primes-noetherian]]), so only
finitely many $V$ meet a fixed affine chart with nonzero coefficient; since $W$
of finite type over a field is quasi-compact, a finite affine cover exhibits
$\operatorname{div}(r)$ as a finite sum, and for merely locally finite type $W$
it is a locally finite sum in the sense of
[[def-algebraic-cycle-and-cycle-group]]. Thus the displayed sum defines an
element of $Z_d(W)$ in the finite-type case and of the locally finite cycle
group in general, and the subgroup $\operatorname{Rat}_d(X)$ is well defined.
items.strategy: The rational-equivalence subgroup is generated by principal divisor cycles on integral subvarieties, using finite sums in the finite-type case and locally finite supporting families otherwise. On an affine chart of an integral supporting subvariety, write a rational function $a/b$ with $a,b$ nonzero. Its nonzero order can occur only at height-one primes containing $ab$. Such primes are minimal over $(ab)$, by the principal-ideal theorem in the domain, and there are finitely many because the ring is Noetherian. A finite affine cover gives global finiteness on a finite-type subvariety; otherwise it gives local finiteness. The local order function is already proved. On a normal subvariety its height-one local rings are DVRs, and the length order is exactly the ordinary Weil order. The quotient is therefore the stated Chow group. Top-dimensional cycles on an integral dimension-$n$ scheme give $A_n(X)=\mathbb Z[X]$, since no dimension-$(n+1)$ subvariety exists; cycles in greater dimensions vanish. The locally finite convention is essential for the non-quasi-compact operations. Stacks42.17/19 gives this exact definition; no unverified Fulton reading is used.

items.title: The cycle associated to a closed subscheme and to a coherent sheaf
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for the going-down
prime-lifting supplier used in flat pullback. Let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over a field; use finite cycles if $X$
is of finite type, and locally finite cycles otherwise. For each integer $d$, a
coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$ whose support has dimension at most $d$ has the
$d$-cycle
$$[\mathcal F]_d=\sum_{\dim V=d}\ell_{\mathcal O_{X,\eta_V}}(\mathcal F_{\eta_V})[V],$$
where $V$ runs over the integral closed subschemes and $\eta_V$ is their generic
point. The sum is locally finite, and finite for finite type $X$; its terms are
precisely the dimension-$d$ components of the support. In any short exact
sequence of coherent sheaves all supported in dimension at most $d$, these
$d$-cycles are additive. No additivity is claimed for the sum of cycles in all
dimensions when the supports change.

For a closed subscheme $Y$, define its fundamental cycle $[Y]$ by summing the
generic lengths at every irreducible component of $Y$. If $Y$ is pure
dimensional of dimension $d$, $[Y]=[\mathcal O_Y]_d$. For reduced $Y$ every
component coefficient is one.

For $X'$ locally of finite type over the same field and flat
$f:X'\to X$ with every nonempty fibre pure of dimension $r$, $[f^{-1}Y]_{d+r}=f^*[Y]_d$
when $Y$ is pure of dimension $d$. If $Y$ is pure of dimension $d$ and the
local equation of an effective Cartier divisor $D$ of $X$ is a nonzerodivisor on
$\mathcal O_Y$, then $D|_Y$ is an effective Cartier divisor and its cycle is the
fundamental $(d-1)$-cycle of $Y\cap D$. The nonzerodivisor condition cannot be
replaced by $Y\not\subset D$: it must exclude every associated point of $Y$,
including embedded ones.
items.strategy: At a dimension-$d$ point of the support of a coherent sheaf supported in dimension at most $d$, localization has zero-dimensional support, so the localized finite module has finite length. There are only finitely many such generic support points. Localization is exact and length is additive, proving additivity for sheaves with the common dimension bound. For an integral or reduced subscheme the generic local rings are fields, giving multiplicity one. For flat pullback, localize at a generic point of a component of the inverse image. A composition series of the finite-length module at the original generic point remains exact after flat tensor, and each simple factor becomes the residue-field fibre module. Additivity of length gives the pulled-back coefficient, including the generic fibre multiplicity. For the divisor assertion, its equation is injective on $\mathcal O_Y$ by hypothesis; its quotient is $\mathcal O_{Y\cap D}$, so the order/length coefficient defining the Cartier cycle is exactly its generic length. Source: Stacks 42.9-42.10 and 42.14, with fixed-dimension bounds essential. Example showing the omitted bound is false: on an integral curve $C$, $0\to\mathcal O_C(-p)\to\mathcal O_C\to\mathcal O_p\to0$ has full support cycles $[C],[C],[p]$, which are not additive in the cycle group.

items.title: Vector bundles and coherent sheaves generate the same K-classes on a regular scheme
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
ample/global-generation and regular-local homological suppliers. Let $X$ be a
regular quasi-projective scheme of finite type over a field. Then the natural
map
$$K^0(X)\longrightarrow K_0(X),\qquad [\mathcal E]\longmapsto[\mathcal E]$$
is an isomorphism. Every coherent sheaf has a finite resolution by finite
locally free sheaves, and its class corresponds to the alternating sum of such
a resolution, independent of the resolution. Consequently this identification
applies to every smooth quasi-projective variety used in the Riemann-Roch
theorem of this page. Regularity alone is not asserted to supply a global
vector-bundle resolution on an arbitrary scheme.
items.strategy:
No coherent extension to a projective closure or unproved FAC input is needed. A quasi-projective immersion $X\to\mathbb P^N_k$ gives the ample invertible sheaf $L=\mathcal O(1)|_X$ by [[lem-very-ample-implies-ample]]. The published [[thm-serre-criterion-ampleness]] applies to this Noetherian $X$, including when $X$ is not proper: for every coherent $F$, $F\otimes L^m$ is globally generated for large $m$. Its finite type and quasi-compactness let finitely many global sections suffice: for every stalk select finitely many generating sections, their cokernel vanishes on a neighbourhood, and finitely many such neighbourhoods cover $X$. Untwisting gives a surjection from a finite sum of $L^{-m}$ onto $F$. All kernels are coherent, so repeat.
Put $n=\dim X$. At each stalk $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, the published regular-local residue-field result and [[lem-local-global-dimension-equals-residue-field-projective-dimension]] give $\operatorname{gldim}R=\dim R\le n$. The syzygy criterion makes the $n$th kernel projective at every stalk, hence locally free: a finite presented sheaf with free stalk is free on a neighbourhood, by lifting a stalk basis and killing the finitely generated kernel and cokernel after shrinking. This terminates the construction in a bounded vector-bundle resolution.
Here is the required global comparison, without treating vector bundles as projective objects of the coherent-sheaf category. Pad two resolutions $E_\bullet,F_\bullet$ of $H$ to length $n$. Choose a vector-bundle cover of $E_0\times_HF_0$; its maps to both degree-zero terms are surjective. Inductively suppose the new resolution has syzygy $K_q$ mapping surjectively to both old syzygies $K^E_q,K^F_q$. Cover the coherent fibre product
$$E_q\times_{K^E_q}K_q\times_{K^F_q}F_q$$
by a vector bundle $G_q$. Its projections to $K_q,E_q,F_q$ are surjective, since all preceding syzygy maps and old covers are surjective. Taking kernels preserves surjectivity onto the next old syzygies, by the snake lemma. At degree $n$ put $G_n=K_n$, locally free by the dimension bound; it maps surjectively onto $E_n,F_n$. Thus a bounded common refinement $G_\bullet$ maps degreewise surjectively to both resolutions, inducing the identity on $H$. The kernel complex of either map is bounded and acyclic, with vector-bundle terms: a surjection between locally free sheaves has locally free kernel because it splits on an affine trivializing neighbourhood. In a bounded acyclic complex of vector bundles, successive kernels from the right endpoint are locally free; its short exact sequences show that its alternating $K^0$ class is zero. Hence the alternating classes of both resolutions equal that of $G_\bullet$.
For additivity, given $0\to H'\to H\to H''\to0$, choose a vector-bundle cover $C\to H''$ and a vector-bundle cover $A\to H\times_{H''}C$. Then $A\to C$ is surjective and $B=\ker(A\to C)$ is a vector bundle; its map $B\to H'$ and $A\to H$ are surjective. This gives the short exact vector-bundle row $0\to B\to A\to C\to0$ over the coherent row. The induced kernel row is exact. Repeat on that kernel row, stopping at degree $n$ when all three syzygies are locally free. We obtain a short exact sequence of bounded vector-bundle resolutions, so their alternating classes are additive term by term. Independence now defines an additive map $G_0(X)\to K^0(X)$ inverse to the natural map, because the alternating class maps to $[H]$ in $G_0$, and a vector bundle has its own degree-zero resolution. AC is inherited exactly through the named global-generation, ample and homological suppliers; no new choice-free assertion is made. Borel-Serre1958 §4 Lemmas8-14 supplies the same full comparison/additivity argument; its FAC input is replaced here by the explicitly published ample criterion. In dimension zero every coherent sheaf is already locally free, so the resolution and comparison arguments reduce to degree zero.

items.title: Pushforward in algebraic K-theory of coherent sheaves
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice, inherited from the
coherence and finiteness suppliers below ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field and let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper
morphism of schemes of finite type over $k$ ([[def-proper-morphism]],
[[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]]); then $Y$ is locally
Noetherian and for every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ all higher
direct images $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ are coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules
([[thm-proper-pushforward-coherent]], [[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]]) and
vanish for all sufficiently large $q$
([[thm-cohomological-dimension-noetherian-scheme]] on the separated Noetherian
preimage of each affine open of $Y$, giving the single global bound
$q>\dim X$). Set
$$f_![\mathcal F]:=\sum_{q\ge0}(-1)^q\,[R^qf_*\mathcal F]\in K_0(Y)$$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]).
Then:

1. $f_!$ is a well-defined homomorphism $K_0(X)\to K_0(Y)$ of abelian groups:
   a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ on
   $X$ induces the long exact sequence of higher direct images
   $0\to f_*\mathcal F'\to f_*\mathcal F\to f_*\mathcal F''\to R^1f_*\mathcal F'\to\cdots$
   ([[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]], [[cor-derived-long-exact-sequence]]),
   whose alternating sum is zero, giving
   $f_![\mathcal F]=f_![\mathcal F']+f_![\mathcal F'']$.
2. (Functoriality) $\operatorname{id}_!=\operatorname{id}$ and
   $(g\circ f)_!=g_!\circ f_!$ for composable proper morphisms: the bounded
   Leray spectral sequence for the composition preserves its total alternating
   class on every page; no degeneration or splitting is asserted
   ([[thm-leray-spectral-sequence-for-sheaf-cohomology]]).
3. (Compatibility with the module structure)
   $f_!(f^*[\mathcal E]\cdot[\mathcal F])=[\mathcal E]\cdot f_![\mathcal F]$
   for $\mathcal E$ locally free on $Y$ and $\mathcal F$ coherent on $X$, i.e.
   the projection formula; this is proved in
   lem-projection-formula-in-algebraic-k-theory. For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$
   and $X$ projective, $f_![\mathcal F]=\chi(X,\mathcal F)$ is the Euler
   characteristic ([[def-euler-characteristic-coherent-sheaf]],
   [[lem-euler-characteristic-additive-short-exact]]).

**Well-definedness.** The sum in the definition is finite because $R^qf_*\mathcal F=0$
for $q>\dim X$: for an affine open $U\subseteq Y$ the preimage $f^{-1}U$ is
separated, Noetherian and of dimension at most $\dim X$, and
[[thm-cohomological-dimension-noetherian-scheme]] bounds its quasi-coherent
cohomology uniformly, the higher direct image being the sheafification of these
local cohomology groups
([[thm-cech-computes-qc-cohomology-separated-scheme-affine-cover]]).
Additivity in short exact sequences is the alternating-sum cancellation in the
bounded long exact sequence of higher direct images, together with the coherence
of every term ([[thm-proper-pushforward-coherent]],
[[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]).
For the composition spectral sequence apply
[[thm-grothendieck-spectral-sequence]] to $f_*$ and $g_*$ on module sheaves.
Module-injective sheaves are flasque
([[lem-injective-modules-flasque-and-ext-of-structure-sheaf]]), their direct
images are flasque, and flasque sheaves are acyclic on every open
([[thm-flasque-sheaves-acyclic]]). As in the module/abelian comparison in
[[thm-leray-spectral-sequence-for-sheaf-cohomology]], this makes them
$g_*$-acyclic and supplies the required acyclicity hypothesis. Functoriality
is then page-invariance of the total alternating class: for composable proper $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ the
$E_2$ page $R^pg_*(R^qf_*\mathcal F)$ is bounded in both directions by the
uniform dimension bounds for $f$, $g$ and $gf$, each differential changes total
degree by one so that the two kernel/image short exact sequences cancel every
image class, and the finite abutment filtration identifies the invariant with
the alternating class of $R^\bullet(g\circ f)_*\mathcal F$
([[thm-leray-spectral-sequence-for-sheaf-cohomology]]); no degeneration is
used. The projection formula is proved separately in
lem-projection-formula-in-algebraic-k-theory, and for $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$
the definition reduces to the Euler characteristic.
items.strategy:
Proper coherence is the named published proper-pushforward theorem. For every affine open $U\subset Y$, $f^{-1}U$ is separated (because $f$ is proper over the affine base), Noetherian and of dimension at most $\dim X$. [[thm-cohomological-dimension-noetherian-scheme]] gives a uniform upper bound on its quasi-coherent cohomology; the higher direct image on $U$ is the sheafification of these local cohomology groups. Hence $R^qf_*F=0$ for the single global bound $q>\dim X$, independently of $U$. This validates a finite sum even for a proper morphism that is not projective. A short exact sequence has a bounded higher-direct-image long exact sequence; its finite alternating class is zero by lengthwise cancellation of image and kernel classes, proving additivity.
For composition $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, apply the published Leray spectral sequence to the restriction of $f$ over $g^{-1}U$ for each open $U\subset Z$. Its restriction-natural pages sheafify to
$$E_2^{p,q}=R^pg_*(R^qf_*F)\Rightarrow R^{p+q}(gf)_*F.$$
Sheafification is exact, so its kernel/image cohomology and finite abutment filtrations remain the indicated sheaves. The module/abelian comparison used here is the general arbitrary-scheme argument in the published Leray proof, not a characteristic-zero shortcut. Proper coherence and the uniform dimension bounds for $f,g,gf$ make the $E_2$ page bounded in both directions. On every page, $E_{r+1}=\ker d_r/\operatorname{im}d_r$ and $d_r$ changes total parity; summing the two short exact kernel/image sequences cancels every image class, so the total alternating class is page-invariant. The finite abutment filtrations give the same alternating class as the higher images of $gf$. Thus $(gf)_!=g_!f_!$. Identity is degree zero. Projection formula is the separately proved local-trivialization lemma; for $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ coherent pushforward is its Euler characteristic. AC and DC are inherited from the exact named injective/cohomology suppliers. Borel-Serre1958 §§3/5 is the full comparison source. No unproved spectral-sequence degeneration is used.

items.title: Proper pushforward of cycles is well defined on Chow groups
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
proper/quasi-finite and scheme base-change suppliers. Let $k$ be a field and let
$f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite type over $k$
([[def-proper-morphism]], [[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]]).
For an integral closed subscheme $V\subseteq X$ with generic point $\eta$, let
$W=\overline{f(V)}\subseteq Y$ with the reduced structure, an integral closed
subscheme ([[def-scheme-theoretic-image]], [[thm-proper-morphism-closed-image]]).
Define
$$f_*[V]:=\begin{cases} [k(V):k(W)]\cdot[W], & \dim W=\dim V,\\ 0, & \dim W<\dim V,\end{cases}$$
where $k(V)$, $k(W)$ are the function fields ([[def-sheaf-total-quotient-rings]])
and $[k(V):k(W)]$ is the extension degree
([[def-extension-degree-and-finite-extension]]), finite because a dominant
morphism $V\to W$ of integral finite-type $k$-schemes with $\dim V=\dim W$ has
algebraic, hence finite, function field extension. Extending $\mathbb Z$-linearly
gives $f_*:Z_d(X)\to Z_d(Y)$ for all $d$. Then:

1. $f_*$ is a homomorphism of graded groups and
   $f_*(\operatorname{Rat}_d(X))\subseteq\operatorname{Rat}_d(Y)$, so it
   descends to $f_*:A_d(X)\to A_d(Y)$
   ([[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]]).
2. (Functoriality) $\operatorname{id}_*=\operatorname{id}$ and
   $(g\circ f)_*=g_*\circ f_*$ for proper $f,g$; the degree is multiplicative in
   towers of finite function-field extensions.
3. (Base change) For a cartesian square with $g$ flat of pure relative dimension $n$
   and proper $f$, the
   compatibility of lem-pushforward-pullback-compatibility-chow holds.
4. (Normalization) If $f$ is finite flat of constant degree $n$ between integral
   schemes of the same dimension, then $f_*[X]=n[Y]$.

Point (1) is the nontrivial assertion: for $W\subseteq X$ integral of dimension
$d+1$ and $r\in k(W)^*$ one has
$$f_*\bigl(\operatorname{div}_W(r)\bigr)=\operatorname{div}_{f(W)}\bigl(N_{k(W)/k(f(W))}(r)\bigr)$$
when $\dim f(W)=\dim W$, and $f_*(\operatorname{div}_W(r))=0$ when
$\dim f(W)<\dim W$; here $N$ is the field norm.
items.strategy:
Complete Stacks42.18.1-18.3/20.3 route, with its determinant/length input supplied explicitly. At a codimension-one point of the image, a proper generically finite morphism is finite nearby: an irreducible component of a positive-dimensional fibre there would have closure of dimension at least the ambient dimension, contradicting proper containment in the integral source. Thus the fibre is finite; openness of the quasi-finite locus and closedness of its proper-image complement give a neighbourhood where the map is proper quasi-finite, hence finite. Reduce the norm formula to a finite extension of one-dimensional local domains $A\subset B$ with fraction fields $K\subset L$.
For two full $A$-lattices $M,M'$ in a finite-dimensional $K$-space, their intersection has finite-colength in each. Define
$$\delta(M,M')=\ell_A(M/(M\cap M'))-\ell_A(M'/(M\cap M')).$$
A common lattice contained in three given lattices proves $\delta(M,M'')=\delta(M,M')+\delta(M',M'')$ by length additivity. Applying a $K$-linear automorphism to both lattices preserves lengths. Hence $g\mapsto\delta(M,gM)$ is a group homomorphism independent of $M$. For a diagonal automorphism of $K^n$ it is the order of its determinant, by the elementary length definition on $A^n$. An elementary transvection preserves a lattice obtained by scaling one standard basis vector to clear its denominator, so its index is zero. Gaussian elimination expresses every invertible matrix as elementary transvections and a diagonal matrix (row swaps are products of these and a diagonal unit), proving
$$\delta(M,gM)=\operatorname{ord}_A(\det g).$$
For multiplication by $r\in L^*$ on the $A$-lattice $B$, its determinant is $N_{L/K}(r)$. Clear a denominator to reduce to $r\in B$; then the index is $\ell_A(B/rB)$. Decomposing this finite-length module over the maximal ideals $q$ of the semilocal $B$ gives
$$\operatorname{ord}_A(N_{L/K}r)=\sum_q[\kappa(q):\kappa(A)]\operatorname{ord}_{B_q}(r).$$
This proves the norm identity even when the rings are not normal or $B$ is not free over $A$.
For a divisor on integral $W$ whose image has the same dimension, this formula proves $f_*\operatorname{div}_W(r)=\operatorname{div}_{f(W)}(Nr)$. If image dimension is smaller by more than one, every divisor component drops dimension and pushes to zero. If it is smaller by one, the coefficient at its generic point is the degree of the principal divisor on the proper generic fibre curve. Take the closure of the graph of $r$ into $\mathbb P^1$; its projection to the curve is proper birational and the norm formula transfers divisors. If the other projection is constant, the divisor is zero. Otherwise it is finite: fibres of a nonconstant map from an integral proper curve are zero-dimensional. It is flat over $\mathbb P^1$, since its finite modules are torsion-free over each target DVR and torsion-free modules over a DVR are flat. Therefore its zero and pole fibres both have degree its generic field degree, giving principal-divisor degree zero. This proves all dimension-drop cases.
Proper composition follows on each integral cycle by multiplying degrees when dimensions agree; if a later image drops dimension both sides are zero. Properness sends a locally finite family of supporting subschemes to a locally finite image family, since the preimage of a quasi-compact target open is quasi-compact. The support-valued norm/divisor identities therefore also descend locally finite rational equivalences. Finite flat degree normalization is generic rank. Flat base change is the separate exact generic-length push-pull lemma, not a multiplicity-one claim.

items.title: Projection formula in algebraic K-theory
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper
morphism of schemes of finite type over a field $k$ ([[def-proper-morphism]],
[[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]]). Let $\mathcal E$ be a
finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent
$\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-coherent-module-scheme]]). Then for every $q\ge0$
there is a canonical isomorphism of coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules
$$R^qf_*\bigl(f^*\mathcal E\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\bigr)\;\cong\;\mathcal E\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}R^qf_*\mathcal F,$$
and consequently, in $K_0(Y)$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]),
$$f_!\bigl(f^*[\mathcal E]\cdot[\mathcal F]\bigr)=[\mathcal E]\cdot f_![\mathcal F],$$
where $f_!$ is the pushforward of
[[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]] and the products are the $K$-theory
module products.
items.strategy: Standard projection formula for higher direct images: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ over which $\mathcal E$ is free, the formula reduces to the case $\mathcal E=\mathcal O_Y$, where it is the naturality of $f_*$; the general case follows by additivity and local trivialization, since locally free sheaves are a direct summand locally ([[lem-internal-hom-fp-qc]] gives the internal-hom adjunction that produces the canonical map, and the trace/evaluation argument shows it is an isomorphism). See Stacks, *Cohomology of Schemes*, Section 30.6 (projection formula) for the complete proof, and Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 5, c (the projection isomorphisms for the direct image functor) with Vakil 245 Class 18 Section 2.2 (Lemma: $f_*(f^*\alpha\cdot\beta)=\alpha\cdot f_*\beta$, proved from $R^if_*(f^*E\otimes F)=E\otimes R^if_*F$). Summing over $q$ with alternating signs gives the $K$-theory identity, since $[\mathcal E]$ acts on $K_0$ by tensor product.

items.title: K-theory of projective space and surjectivity for projections
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field.

1. In $K^0(\mathbb P^n_k)=K_0(\mathbb P^n_k)$
   ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]],
   [[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]) the classes
   $[\mathcal O(i)]$, $0\le i\le n$, form a $\mathbb Z$-basis; equivalently
   $K_0(\mathbb P^n)=\mathbb Z^{n+1}$ generated by the twisting sheaves
   ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]],
   [[thm-twisting-sheaf-invertible-standard-graded]]).
2. For every locally Noetherian $k$-scheme $Y$ and every $n\ge0$, the
   exterior-product map
   $$K_0(Y)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K_0(\mathbb P^n_k)\longrightarrow K_0(\mathbb P^n_k\times_kY)$$
   is surjective; here $K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)$ is the Grothendieck group of
   coherent sheaves
   ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]])
   and the product is
   $[\mathcal F]\times[\mathcal G]\mapsto[p_Y^*\mathcal F\otimes p_{\mathbb P}^*\mathcal G]$
   ([[lem-tensor-qc-modules-quasi-coherent]],
   [[lem-pullback-qc-module-quasi-coherent]]).
3. More generally, if $\mathcal E$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module
   of rank $r+1$, the projective bundle $\mathbb P(\mathcal E)$ has
   $K_0(\mathbb P(\mathcal E))$ equal to the image of
   $\bigoplus_{a=0}^r K_0(Y)$ under
   $(\alpha_a)\mapsto\sum_a q^*\alpha_a\otimes[\mathcal O(a)]$; this is
   generation by twists, without treating coherent $K_0(Y)$ as a
   tensor-product ring on a singular base, via the relative-diagonal Koszul
   computation; no global cell decomposition of a nontrivial bundle is assumed
   ([[def-projective-bundle-scheme]]).
items.strategy:
For a rank-$r$ bundle $E$ and $q:P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(E)\to Y$, use the relative diagonal in $P\times_Y P$, with tautological line $L_1$ on the first factor and quotient $Q_2$ on the second. Its equation is the section of $L_1^\vee\otimes Q_2$ induced by $L_1\to q^*E\to Q_2$. On two affine fibre charts it is the sequence of differences of the $r-1$ fibre coordinates, so its Koszul complex resolves the diagonal. For every coherent $F$ on $P$, that Koszul complex remains exact after tensor with $\operatorname{pr}_1^*F$: the differences are a regular sequence on the polynomial module obtained from $F$, by successive evaluation in the second fibre coordinates. Its terms are $\operatorname{pr}_1^*(F(-j))\otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*\bigwedge^jQ^\vee$. Push to the second factor; flat base change and the projection formula, checked on the finite standard projective affine Čech cover, give
$$[F]=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}(-1)^j q^*q_![F(-j)]\otimes[\bigwedge^jQ^\vee].$$
The tautological dual exact sequence gives $[\bigwedge^jQ^\vee]=\sum_{a=0}^j(-1)^a q^*[\bigwedge^{j-a}E^\vee][\mathcal O(a)]$, by its exterior filtration. Thus these terms are sums of $q^*$ of coherent classes tensored with $\mathcal O(a)$ for $0\le a<r$. This works on locally Noetherian bases: higher direct images are coherent locally and vanish above fibre dimension, and the equality is the global sheaf/Čech computation, not gluing local Grothendieck-group identities. Dualizing $E$ gives the quotient convention. This proves both generation assertions including nontrivial projective bundles.
For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$, independence of $\mathcal O(0),\ldots,\mathcal O(n)$ follows by pairing with the Euler characteristics of twists $\mathcal O(-j)$ for $j=0,\ldots,n$: the matrix $\chi(\mathcal O(a-j))=\binom{n+a-j}{n}$ is upper triangular with diagonal one, since $-n\le a-j<0$ gives zero. The standard projective affine Čech complex computes these Euler characteristics. Generation plus this unimodular pairing proves the asserted basis. AC is inherited from coherent cohomology. Borel-Serre §9 and Vakil19 supply comparison for the trivial bundle case; their cellular argument alone does not prove the general-bundle claim. The diagonal calculation is given in full here and agrees with the later smooth-base helper.

items.title: Flat pullback of cycles is well defined on Chow groups
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
proper/quasi-finite and scheme base-change suppliers. Let $k$ be a field and let
$f:X\to Y$ be a flat morphism of schemes locally of finite type over $k$
([[def-flat-morphism-schemes]]) all of whose nonempty fibres have pure dimension
$n$ ([[def-scheme-theoretic-fibre]],
[[def-dimension-noetherian-topological-space]]); for instance $f$ smooth of
relative dimension $n$ ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]],
[[def-relative-dimension-smooth-morphism]], [[lem-smooth-fibres-smooth]]) or an
open immersion with $n=0$. For an integral closed subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ let
$f^{-1}(V)=V\times_Y X$ be the scheme-theoretic preimage and let $[f^{-1}(V)]$
be its cycle ([[lem-cycle-of-a-closed-subscheme]]). Extending linearly gives
$f^*:Z_d(Y)\to Z_{d+n}(X)$. Then:

1. If $f^{-1}(V)$ is nonempty, it is equidimensional of dimension
   $\dim V+n$; if it is empty, $f^*[V]=0$. In both cases $f^*[V]$ is a
   pure $(d+n)$-cycle; this is the only place the pure-fibre-dimension
   hypothesis is used.
2. $f^*(\operatorname{Rat}_d(Y))\subseteq\operatorname{Rat}_{d+n}(X)$: for an
   integral closed subscheme $W\subseteq Y$ of dimension $d+1$ and
   $r\in k(W)^*$, if $W_j$ are the reduced irreducible components of
   $f^{-1}(W)$ with generic lengths $n_j$, then
   $f^*(\operatorname{div}_W(r))=\sum_j n_j\operatorname{div}_{W_j}(r|_{W_j})$,
   pushed to $X$, and the right-hand side lies in
   $\operatorname{Rat}_{d+n}(X)$.
3. Consequently $f^*$ descends to a graded homomorphism
   $f^*:A_d(Y)\to A_{d+n}(X)$
   ([[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]]).
4. (Functoriality) $\operatorname{id}^*=\operatorname{id}$ and
   $(g\circ f)^*=f^*\circ g^*$ for composable flat morphisms of the stated kind;
   if $f$ is an open immersion then $f^*$ is the restriction of cycles.
5. (Localization) If $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is an open immersion and
   $i:Z=X\setminus U\hookrightarrow X$ the complementary reduced closed
   subscheme, the sequence
   $A_*(Z)\xrightarrow{i_*}A_*(X)\xrightarrow{j^*}A_*(U)\to0$ is exact (using
   [[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]] for $i_*$).
items.strategy:
Use the complete generic-length calculation of Stacks42.13-42.14 and 42.20.1-20.2. Flat finite-presentation maps are open; therefore every component over an integral base dominates it. At its generic point the fibre has dimension $r$, so the dimension/transcendence formula gives dimension $\dim W+r$. This proves the pure-dimension assertion. For flat local rings $A\to B$ and a finite-length $A$-module $M$, a composition series and flat tensor give $\ell_B(B\otimes_AM)=\ell_A(M)\ell_B(B/\mathfrak m_AB)$ when those lengths are finite. Applying this to generic support stalks proves flat pullback of a coherent fixed-dimensional cycle. Iterating the same identity proves flat composition, including fibre multiplicities.
For divisor descent, inspect the generic point of a codimension-one component over a divisor of integral $W$. Its local flat map $A\to B$ has $A$ a one-dimensional domain and $\mathfrak m_AB$ an ideal of definition. Write the rational function as $x/y$, with $x,y\in A$ nonzero. Flatness makes each a nonzerodivisor in $B$. A prime filtration of the one-dimensional $B$-module $B$ gives
$$\ell_B(B/xB)=\sum_{q\text{ minimal}}\ell_{B_q}(B_q)\ell_B(B/(x,q)).$$
To justify the filtration computation in the presence of finite-length filtration factors, use the additive invariant $\ell\operatorname{coker}(x)-\ell\ker(x)$: it is additive by the kernel-cokernel long exact sequence, is zero on finite-length factors, and equals the length quotient on $B$, since $x$ is injective. The remaining factors are rank-one modules over the one-dimensional domains $B/q$, whose invariant is their order function; a generic composition filtration produces their multiplicities $\ell_{B_q}(B_q)$. Subtract the identical formula for $y$. This proves the component-weighted divisor identity in the statement. Over a component mapping to the generic point of $W$ both coefficients are zero, since $r$ is a unit there. Every pulled-back principal divisor is thus a sum of principal divisors on reduced components with the generic-length weights. Their supporting inverse images form a locally finite family, so this is rational equivalence with the correct support convention.
For localization, lift cycles from the open by closure. Lift each supporting subvariety of a rational equivalence by closure and use its identical function field; subtract its extended principal divisor. The remaining cycle is supported on the closed complement, proving exactness. Local finiteness of these closures follows because every quasi-compact open in the Noetherian scheme has quasi-compact intersection with the given open, and meets only finitely many supports. No reducedness of the flat preimage is assumed.

items.title: Two-dimensional tame-symbol reciprocity and divisor commutation
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
proper/quasi-finite and scheme base-change suppliers. Let $A$ be a
two-dimensional local domain essentially of finite type over a field and
$f,g\in\operatorname{Frac}(A)^\times$. For each height-one prime $q$, define
$\partial_q(f,g)$ by normalization and norms of the DVR symbols
$(-1)^{v(f)v(g)}f^{v(g)}/g^{v(f)}$ reduced in the residue fields. Then
$\sum_q\operatorname{ord}_{A/q}(\partial_q(f,g))=0$. The difference between two
orders of rational-section intersection is consequently a sum of divisors
of these symbols; for two section zero schemes the relations can be chosen
on their common intersection. This proves
well-definedness of first Chern operators and Cartier Gysin on rational
equivalence and commutation of two Cartier Gysins.
items.strategy:
Source: full Stacks42.2-42.6 and 42.27-42.30, with the finite-type normalization simplification. Define $e(M,a,b)=\ell(\ker(a)/bM)-\ell(\ker(b)/aM)$ for the two-periodic complex with $abM=0$ and closed-point-supported homology. The long exact homology sequence proves additivity. If $M$ has finite length then $\ell\ker(a)=\ell M-\ell aM$ and $\ell\ker(b)=\ell M-\ell bM$, so $e=0$. Finite-length changes in a module therefore change no $e$. The nilpotent calculation required for the lattice case is as follows. For an endomorphism $t$ with $t^NM=0$, set $K_i=\ker t^i$, $a_i=\ell(K_i/t^{N-i}M)$, $b_i=\ell(K_i/tK_{i+1})$, $c_i=\ell(K_1/t^iK_{i+1})$. Finite-length homology makes these lengths finite for $0<i<N$; the cases $i=0,N$ have zero Herbrand invariant. The identity $K_i\cap t^jM=t^jK_{i+j}$ yields the exact sequences
$$0\to K_1/t^{N-i-1}K_{N-i}\to K_{i+1}/t^{N-i-1}M\xrightarrow{t}K_i/t^{N-i}M\to K_i/tK_{i+1}\to0,$$
$$0\to K_i/tK_{i+1}\to K_{i+1}/tK_{i+2}\xrightarrow{t^i}K_1/t^{i+1}K_{i+2}\to K_1/t^iK_{i+1}\to0.$$
They give $c_{N-i-1}-a_{i+1}+a_i-b_i=0$ and $b_i-b_{i+1}+c_{i+1}-c_i=0$. With $b_0=c_0=0$, the latter gives $b_i=c_i$. Thus $a_{i+1}-a_i=b_{N-i-1}-b_i$; summing gives $a_i=a_{N-i}$, which is exactly $e(M,t^i,t^{N-i})=0$. This supplies the formerly unsupported equality of the two lattice parity defects.
For multiplication of the first differential by $x$ with $M/xM$ supported only at the closed point, remove the $x$-power torsion of $M$, which has finite length and hence zero invariant. On the remaining module $x$ is injective, $\ker(xa)=\ker a$, and
$$0\to aM/xaM\to\ker b/(xaM)\to\ker b/aM\to0.$$
Length additivity gives $e(M,xa,b)=e(M,a,b)-e(aM,0,x)$. Interchanging parities gives the analogous second-differential identity with a plus sign. For a module of generic length $h$ at a height-one prime, a generic composition filtration, lifted to lattices with finite-length kernel/cokernel defects, gives $e(M,0,x)=h\operatorname{ord}_{A/q}(x)$; finite-length factors contribute zero and rank-one factors are the order definition. Applying the multiplier identities to $a=u\pi^e,b=v\pi^f$ therefore gives the exact formula
$$e(M,a,b)=-f\operatorname{ord}_{A/q}(u)+e\operatorname{ord}_{A/q}(v).$$
Clear denominators of $\pi,u,v$ by a multiplier nonzero at $q$; the same two identities show that the correction on the left is the order of the identical extra symbol factor on the right. Thus the computation is valid for elements in $A_q$, not just in $A$.
Normalize the two-dimensional finite-type local domain; its normalization is finite and semilocal. In a normal local factor every height-one localization is a DVR. For nonzero $a,b$, the complex on $A/(ab)$ is acyclic by cancellation of $a,b$ in the domain. Map $A/(ab)$ to the direct sum of its image lattices $M_q$ in $A_q/(ab)$ over primes dividing $ab$; this is an isomorphism at each nonmaximal point of the support, so its kernel and cokernel have finite length. Hence $\sum_qe(M_q,a,b)=0$. Write $a=u_q\pi_q^{e_q}$, $b=v_q\pi_q^{f_q}$. The preceding identities, clearing denominators when necessary, give $e(M_q,a,b)=-\operatorname{ord}_{A/q}(u_q^{f_q}v_q^{-e_q})$; the constant sign in the tame symbol has order zero. This proves reciprocity in the normal case. For the original domain, the norm-order formula for the finite normalization identifies the sum of these local identities with its desired sum, weighting residue extensions correctly. More precisely, if $B$ is the finite normalization of the local $A$, multiply each two-dimensional local reciprocity identity for $B_{\mathfrak n}$ by $[\kappa(\mathfrak n):\kappa(\mathfrak m_A)]$. For each height-one $q\subset A$, the one-dimensional norm-order identity on the finite normalizations of $A/q$ identifies the sum over chains $Q\subset\mathfrak n$ in $B$ above $q\subset\mathfrak m_A$ with $\operatorname{ord}_{A/q}\prod_{Q|q}N_{\kappa(Q)/\kappa(q)}\partial_Q(f,g)$. Summing the local identities therefore yields the claimed identity on $A$. The explicit determinant/lattice proof of that norm-order identity is the proper-pushforward supplier; it also proves consistency with the length-order definition on nonnormal height-one rings. Bilinearity and additive order extend the result from elements to fractions.
To apply it geometrically, choose rational sections of two line bundles and local generators along their codimension-one divisor components; write them as $f_q,g_q$ times these generators. At each codimension-two point the difference between the two iterated divisor cycles is the sum of the local orders of $\partial_q(f_q,g_q)$, by expanding the section divisors in those generators. The local reciprocity identity makes this the cycle $\sum_q\operatorname{div}_{\overline q}(\partial_q(f_q,g_q))$. Choose a generator to equal the regular section on components outside its zero scheme. There the ratio to the chosen generator is one, hence the corresponding symbol is one, so this principal-divisor discrepancy is supported on the common zero scheme. It is a rational equivalence there and proves Cartier commutation. With the second line bundle trivial and its rational section a rational function, its Chern operation is zero; the same calculation says Cartier Gysin kills principal divisors. Without a support restriction the double-section calculation proves descent of the first Chern operation. This is the exact local key-lemma use needed by the following items.

items.title: Proper pushforward and flat pullback commute in a fibre square
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
proper/quasi-finite and scheme base-change suppliers. Let $k$ be a field and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc} X' & \xrightarrow{g'} & X\\ \downarrow f' & & \downarrow f\\ Y' & \xrightarrow{g} & Y\end{array}$$
be a cartesian square of schemes locally of finite type over $k$
([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]), with $f$ proper (hence $f'$
proper, [[lem-proper-stable-base-change]]) and $g$ flat of relative dimension
$n$ with all fibres of pure dimension $n$ (hence $g'$ flat of relative dimension
$n$, [[lem-flat-morphisms-stable-base-change]]). Then the two graded
homomorphisms $A_d(X)\to A_{d+n}(Y')$ agree:
$$g^*\circ f_*\;=\;f'_*\circ g'^*,$$
where $f_*,f'_*$ are proper pushforwards
([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]) and $g^*,g'^*$ are flat
pullbacks ([[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]]).
items.strategy:
Use the complete generic-length proof of Stacks42.15.1, retaining all nilpotent multiplicities. First, for a coherent sheaf $F$ supported in dimension at most $d$, proper pushforward satisfies $f_*[F]_d=[f_*F]_d$. To prove this, inspect a generic point $\eta$ of an image component of dimension $d$. Every point of the support over $\eta$ is generic of a dimension-$d$ support component, since support dimension is at most $d$; the fibre is therefore finite. Proper quasi-finite finiteness gives a finite map on a neighbourhood of $\eta$. A composition series over the generic Artinian local rings gives
$$\ell_{\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}}((f_*F)_\eta)=\sum_{\xi\mapsto\eta}[\kappa(\xi):\kappa(\eta)]\ell_{\mathcal O_{X,\xi}}(F_\xi).$$
If the image dimension is smaller than $d$, both $d$-cycles are zero. Flat pullback satisfies $g^*[F]_d=[g^*F]_{d+r}$ by the previously proved flat length computation. Finally $g^*f_*F\cong f'_*g'^*F$ for flat base change: on an affine open of $Y$, a finite affine open cover of the proper preimage has affine finite intersections (the proper map is separated); the associated Čech complex computes degree-zero sections, and flat tensor with the new affine base commutes with kernels. These natural isomorphisms agree under localization and glue. Apply the three identities to $F=\mathcal O_V$ for each integral cycle $[V]$, then extend linearly (locally finitely in the locally finite type convention). No coefficient is assumed to be one merely because a morphism is flat. Properness and flatness are preserved under base change by the exact published suppliers, giving the operation's typing.

items.title: Intersection with an invertible sheaf and the first Chern class
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
proper/quasi-finite and scheme base-change suppliers. Let $k$ be a field and
let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$. Let $L$ be an invertible
$\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-invertible-sheaf]]).

1. **Integral case.** Let $W\subseteq X$ be integral of dimension $n$, with
   function field $k(W)$ ([[def-sheaf-total-quotient-rings]],
   [[def-field-of-fractions]]), and let $s$ be a nonzero rational section of
   $L|_W$ ([[def-rational-section-line-bundle]]). The **Weil divisor of $s$** is
   $$\operatorname{div}_L(s)=\sum_{Z\subseteq W}\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{W,Z}}(s)[Z]\in Z_{n-1}(W),$$
   the sum over the codimension-one integral closed subschemes $Z\subseteq W$,
   with the order function of [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]]
   read on a local generator of $L$ at the generic point of $Z$; the sum is
   locally finite, and finite if $W$ is of finite type. The **first Chern class** $c_1(L)\cap[W]:=[\operatorname{div}_L(s)]\in A_{n-1}(W)$
   is independent of the chosen nonzero rational section (two such differ by a
   rational function, whose divisor is rationally equivalent to zero), and
   therefore defines a codimension-one Chow class; on a smooth $W$ this is the
   first Chern class in its Chow ring.
2. **General case.** For an integral closed subscheme $i:W\hookrightarrow X$ of
   dimension $d+1$ set
   $c_1(L)\cap[W]:=i_*\bigl(c_1(i^*L)\cap[W]\bigr)\in A_d(X)$, where $i_*$ is
   the proper pushforward ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]);
   extend $\mathbb Z$-linearly. The resulting operation
   $c_1(L)\cap-:A_{d+1}(X)\to A_d(X)$ is well defined on Chow groups (this is
   the content of the next two references) and graded.

**Basic properties.** (i)
$c_1(L\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}N)\cap\alpha=(c_1(L)+c_1(N))\cap\alpha$ and
$c_1(\mathcal O_X)\cap\alpha=0$ for all $\alpha$. (ii) If $X$ is pure of
dimension $d+1$ and a global section $s$ of $L$ is a nonzerodivisor on
$\mathcal O_X$, its zero scheme $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor and
$c_1(L)\cap[X]=[D]$ in $A_d(X)$. More generally the same formula on a
pure-dimensional closed subscheme $Y$ requires $s|_Y$ to be a nonzerodivisor on
$\mathcal O_Y$. (iii) $c_1(L)\cap-$ commutes with proper pushforward and flat
pullback: for $f:X\to Y$ proper,
$f_*(c_1(f^*L)\cap\alpha)=c_1(L)\cap f_*\alpha$, and for $f$ flat of relative
dimension $n$, $f^*(c_1(L)\cap\alpha)=c_1(f^*L)\cap f^*\alpha$. (iv) $c_1(L)$
depends only on the isomorphism class of $L$.

**Cartier Gysin.** For a section $s$ of $L$ with zero scheme
$j:D\hookrightarrow X$, after any base change define
$j^!:A_m(X')\to A_{m-1}(D')$ on integral $V\subset X'$ by the Cartier divisor
of $s|_V$ if $V$ is not contained in $D'$, and by $c_1(L|_V)\cap[V]$ if it is;
push this class from $D'\cap V$ to $D'$. This works even when the pulled-back
zero divisor is not Cartier. It commutes with proper pushforward and flat
pullback, two Cartier Gysins commute, and
$j^!j_*\beta=c_1(L|_D)\cap\beta$.

**Well-definedness.** All the constructions above are local in the integral
cycle, so they are defined for locally finite cycles as well. In the integral
case, a nonzero rational section $s$ of $L|_W$ is a rational multiple of a local
generator, so the order function of
[[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]] is defined at the generic
point of every codimension-one integral closed subscheme $Z\subseteq W$, and
only finitely many $Z$ meeting any fixed affine chart receive a nonzero order: on that chart $W$ is a
Noetherian domain and $s$ is represented by a fraction whose numerator and
denominator vanish on only finitely many height-one primes, exactly as in the
finiteness discussion of [[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]].
The class $[\operatorname{div}_L(s)]$ is independent of $s$ because the ratio of
two rational sections is a rational function of $k(W)^*$ and principal divisors
lie in $\operatorname{Rat}_{n-1}(W)$; this is the definition of rational
equivalence. In the general case the operation is extended by proper pushforward
along $i$ and by linearity; that it descends through rational equivalence on $X$
is the content of [[lem-two-dimensional-tame-symbol-reciprocity]] (the tame
symbol reciprocity that controls the difference of two iterated Cartier
intersections) together with the facts that proper pushforward and flat
pullback each descend to Chow groups
([[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]],
[[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]). Property (ii) is the cycle
computation of [[lem-cycle-of-a-closed-subscheme]]. For (iii), the flat-pullback
identity is the generic-length calculation in [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]]
applied to the divisor cycle; for proper pushforward, trivializing the line
bundle at codimension-one generic points reduces the identity to the norm-order
formula in [[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]. Both identities
are checked on integral cycles and extend linearly. Property (iv) follows
because an isomorphism of invertible sheaves identifies their local generators
and hence the resulting divisor coefficients.
items.strategy: A rational section exists by trivializing the line at the integral generic point. A ratio of choices is a rational function, so the order-function identity changes its divisor only by a principal divisor. Product sections give additivity. The cycle of a regular section is given by lengths of its one-dimensional local quotient by the equation, agreeing with the order definition. Proper and flat compatibilities are the norm-order and flat-length formulas already established for cycle operations; for cycles contained in the zero scheme they give the first Chern projection and pullback identities instead. Descent on rational equivalence uses [[lem-two-dimensional-tame-symbol-reciprocity]]: the rational-section intersection discrepancy is a sum of principal divisors and is zero in Chow. Cartier Gysin has the same two cycle cases. Its image of a principal divisor is the intersection with $c_1(1)=0$, by the same symbol calculation supported on $D$. Hence it descends. The support-controlled double-section discrepancy proves commutation of Cartier Gysins. On a cycle already on $D$, the definition gives exactly $j^!j_*\beta=c_1(L|_D)\beta$. Thus the divisor Gysin required by specialization is supplied explicitly.

items.title: Localization and homotopy invariance for Chow groups
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
proper/quasi-finite and scheme base-change suppliers. For a closed immersion
$j:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with complement $u:U\hookrightarrow T$,
$A_m(Z)\xrightarrow{j_*}A_m(T)\xrightarrow{u^*}A_m(U)\to0$ is exact. Projection
$T\times\mathbb A^r\to T$ gives an isomorphism
$A_m(T)\cong A_{m+r}(T\times\mathbb A^r)$. These statements hold for finite type
schemes over a field and locally finite cycles on locally finite type schemes.
items.strategy: Source: Stacks 42.19.3, 42.32 and 42.36.3. For localization, close each integral cycle of $U$ in $T$ to prove surjectivity. If the restriction of a cycle is a sum of principal divisors, close their supporting integral subvarieties in $T$ and extend the same rational functions; their divisors restrict to the specified divisors on $U$. Subtracting them leaves a cycle supported on $Z$, proving exactness. This also proves that locally finite sums can be used. For $\mathbb A^1_T$, surjectivity of pullback is proved on each integral cycle $V$: if $V$ is the whole line over its integral image, it is a pullback; otherwise over the generic point of its image it is the divisor of a polynomial in the line coordinate, and subtracting that principal divisor leaves cycles over a smaller closed subset. Noetherian induction finishes. Pullback is injective since the Cartier Gysin for the zero section is a left inverse (on a pulled-back cycle it cuts the coordinate by a nonzerodivisor and gives its original fundamental cycle). Iterate this argument for $\mathbb A^r_T$.  For injectivity in rank $r$, compose the Cartier Gysins of the $r$ coordinate-zero divisors; each cuts the corresponding polynomial coordinate on every pulled-back integral cycle and their composition is a left inverse. This is an argument with divisor Gysin only, independent of higher-codimension Gysin or Chern classes.

items.title: Chow groups of projective space by cellular decomposition
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
proper/quasi-finite and scheme base-change suppliers. Let $k$ be a field and
$n\ge0$. Then for every $d$:
$$A_d(\mathbb P^n_k)=\begin{cases}\mathbb Z\cdot[\mathbb P^d], & 0\le d\le n,\\ 0, & \text{otherwise},\end{cases}$$
where $\mathbb P^d\subseteq\mathbb P^n$ is a $d$-dimensional linear subspace and
$[\mathbb P^d]$ its class
([[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]],
[[def-algebraic-cycle-and-cycle-group]]). In particular the degree homomorphism
$$\deg:A_0(\mathbb P^n_k)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\mathbb Z,\qquad \sum_x m_x[x]\longmapsto\sum_x m_x[\kappa(x):k],$$
is an isomorphism; its inverse sends $1$ to $[\mathbb P^0]$ for any $k$-rational
point, and every $0$-cycle whose support consists of $k$-rational points has
class $(\sum_x m_x)\,[\mathbb P^0]$. For $k=\mathbb C$ this is the classical
cellular decomposition. More generally,
$A_d(\mathbb A^n_k)=\mathbb Z$ for $d=n$ and $A_d(\mathbb A^n_k)=0$ otherwise:
homotopy invariance shifts degrees by $n$, and $A_*(\operatorname{Spec}k)$ is
$\mathbb Z$ in degree $0$, so every cycle on affine space of dimension less than $n$ is rationally
equivalent to zero. For $n=1$, a closed point of degree greater than one is
the principal divisor of its monic irreducible polynomial; linear polynomials
suffice for rational points.
items.strategy: First [[lem-chow-localization-and-vector-bundle-homotopy]] gives $A_d(\mathbb A^n_k)=A_{d-n}(\operatorname{Spec}k)$, equal to $\mathbb Z$ for $d=n$ and zero otherwise. The degree is shifted by $n$, not left in degree zero. For the hyperplane $\mathbb P^{n-1}\subset\mathbb P^n$, localization then shows that every $d$-cycle with $d<n$ is a pushforward from the hyperplane. Induction on $n$ generates $A_d(\mathbb P^n)$ by the class of a $k$-linear $\mathbb P^d$; for $d=n$ the top cycle group is already $\mathbb Z[\mathbb P^n]$, with no rational equivalences in that dimension. To prove independence for $d\le n$, apply $d$ first-Chern cap operators for $\mathcal O(1)$ and then proper pushforward to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. On the linear $\mathbb P^d$, successive coordinate hyperplanes are Cartier cuts ending in a rational point, so this homomorphism sends its class to one. A cyclic group with a generator mapped to one is infinite cyclic. For any closed point $x$, proper pushforward sends $[x]$ to $[\kappa(x):k]$ by definition, hence $[x]=[\kappa(x):k][\mathbb P^0]$ in this group. This proves all generators, their independence, vanishing outside $0\le d\le n$, and the degree formula without using the later projective bundle formula. Source: Stacks42.19/32 and the complete cap/localization argument above; the old unresolved kernel guess and incorrect affine-degree assertion are removed.

items.title: Deformation to the normal cone and specialization
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the smooth
normal-sequence suppliers. For a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ with
ideal $\mathcal I$, put
$C_XY=\operatorname{Spec}_X(\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1})$
and $M=\operatorname{Bl}_{X\times\{\infty\}}(Y\times\mathbb P^1)$. Let
$B=\operatorname{Bl}_XY$ be the strict transform of $Y\times\{\infty\}$. The
fibre at infinity is the sum $M_\infty=B+\mathbb P(C_XY\oplus1)$ of effective
Cartier divisors, whose intersection is $\mathbb P(C_XY)$; this is a union with
a common boundary, not a disjoint union. Projectivized cones here use the lines
convention $\operatorname{Proj}(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathcal I}\mathcal O_Y[S])$.
Off infinity $M\cong Y\times\mathbb A^1$, and $D_i:=M\setminus B$ has special
fibre $C_XY$ and ordinary fibres $Y$. It is flat over $\mathbb P^1$. The
**specialization** $\sigma_i:A_m(Y)\to A_m(C_XY)$ is obtained by extending the
flat pullback of a cycle to $D_i$, then taking Cartier Gysin at infinity. It
sends an integral $[V]$ to the fundamental cycle $[C_{X\cap V}V]$ pushed to
$C_XY$. For a regular immersion of codimension $d$, the normal cone equals the
rank-$d$ normal bundle $N_{X/Y}$. The construction works for finite type
schemes over a field, with locally finite cycles in the locally finite type
case.

**Well-definedness.** The charts of $M$ near infinity are computed directly:
over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ with
$X=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and $t$ the coordinate vanishing at infinity, the
$t$-chart of the blowup is the affine blowup algebra
$A[t,I/t]=\sum_{n\ge0}t^{-n}I^n[t]\subseteq A[t,t^{-1}]$, and multiplication by
$t$ is injective with quotient $\operatorname{gr}_IA$; in the chart of a
generator $a\in I$ the ring is $A[I/a][t/a]$, and $t=a(t/a)$ exhibits the fibre
at $t=0$ as the sum of the exceptional divisor $a=0$ and the strict transform
$t/a=0$, whose charts are $\operatorname{Bl}_XY$ and whose intersection is
$\operatorname{Proj}\operatorname{gr}_IA$. This identifies the fibre at
infinity as the stated union of effective Cartier divisors, without assuming
$Y$ integral or the centre Cartier, and shows that, away from infinity, $M\setminus B\cong Y\times\mathbb A^1$,
while its special fibre is $C_XY$; the charts are torsion-free over $k[t]$ (or polynomial
over the affine blowup algebras), and a torsion-free module over the principal
ideal domain $k[t]$ is flat, giving flatness of $M$ over $\mathbb P^1$
(compare the chart computation of
[[lem-smooth-immersion-normal-sequence-and-deformation-charts]]). Localization
for the pair $C_XY\hookrightarrow M\setminus B$ gives a lift of the pulled-back
cycle class to $D_i$, and two lifts differ by a class supported on $C_XY$; the
Cartier Gysin at infinity kills that difference because the normal line of the
infinity fibre is trivial, so $j^!j_*\gamma=c_1(\mathcal O)\cap\gamma=0$ by the
basic property $c_1(\mathcal O_X)=0$ of
[[def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class]]; hence
$\sigma_i$ is well defined on Chow classes. On an integral cycle $[V]$ the
closure of $V\times\mathbb A^1$ in the $t$-chart is
$\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_V[t,I\mathcal O_V/t]$, and cutting by $t$
produces $\operatorname{gr}_{I\mathcal O_V}\mathcal O_V$, which is the
fundamental cycle of the normal cone $C_{X\cap V}V$ with its generic lengths;
for a regular sequence generating $I$,
[[lem-regular-sequence-associated-graded-polynomial]] identifies
$\operatorname{gr}_IA$ with $\operatorname{Sym}_{A/I}(I/I^2)$, so the cone is
the rank-$d$ normal bundle of
[[lem-smooth-immersion-normal-sequence-and-deformation-charts]].
items.strategy:
Candidate source locators: Stacks 42.53 and 42.48.1, with Vakil Class14 as a sketch comparison only. Near infinity write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and let $t$ vanish at infinity. The $t$-chart of the blowup has ring $A[t,I/t]=\sum_{n\ge0}t^{-n}I^n[t]\subset A[t,t^{-1}]$. Multiplication by $t$ is injective and its quotient is $\operatorname{gr}_I A$. In the chart of a generator $a\in I$, the ring is $A[I/a][t/a]$ (the affine blowup algebra means the subring of $A_a$, including its usual torsion removal); $t=a(t/a)$, so its fibre is the sum of the exceptional divisor $a=0$ and the strict transform $t/a=0$. The strict transform charts are exactly $\operatorname{Bl}_XY$, and its intersection with the exceptional divisor is $\operatorname{Proj}\operatorname{gr}_I A$. This proves the fibre and open-chart assertions, even for singular $Y$. The charts embed in $A[t,t^{-1}]$ or are polynomial rings over the affine blowup algebras, and are torsion-free as $k[t]$-modules; all nonzero polynomials act injectively. A torsion-free module over the PID $k[t]$ is flat (every finitely generated submodule is free and the module is their filtered union). The infinity charts and ordinary product charts thus prove flatness without assuming $Y$ integral or misidentifying the centre as Cartier.
Localization gives a lift of the pulled-back class to $D_i$; two lifts differ by a class supported on $C_XY$. Cartier Gysin kills this difference because the normal line to the infinity fibre is trivial: $j^!j_*\gamma=c_1(1)\gamma=0$. Thus specialization is well defined on Chow classes. On $[V]$, closure in the $t$-chart is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_V[t,I\mathcal O_V/t]$; cutting by $t$ produces $\operatorname{gr}_{I\mathcal O_V}\mathcal O_V$, giving the asserted cone cycle with its generic lengths. For a regular sequence, the monomials in its generators identify $\operatorname{gr}_I A$ with $\operatorname{Sym}_{A/I}(I/I^2)$, hence the cone is $N_{X/Y}$.
