items.title: The projective bundle formula for Chow groups
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
proper/quasi-finite and scheme base-change suppliers. Let $k$ be a field, let
$X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$, and let $\mathcal E$ be a
finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of rank $r\ge1$
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]). Let
$$\pi:\mathbb P(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{Proj}_X\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)\longrightarrow X$$
be the projective bundle in the quotient convention, with tautological quotient
$\pi^*\mathcal E\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(\mathcal E)}(1)$
([[def-projective-bundle-scheme]],
[[def-relative-proj-quasi-coherent-graded-algebra]],
[[thm-projective-bundle-represents-line-quotients]]), and put
$\xi:=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$
([[def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class]]); $\pi$ is
smooth of relative dimension $r-1$
([[def-relative-dimension-smooth-morphism]]), so flat pullback $\pi^*$ is
defined ([[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]], [[lem-smooth-fibres-smooth]]). Then
for every $d\in\mathbb Z$ the map
$$\bigoplus_{i=0}^{r-1}A_{d+i}(X)\longrightarrow A_{d+r-1}\bigl(\mathbb P(\mathcal E)\bigr),\qquad (\alpha_0,\dots,\alpha_{r-1})\longmapsto\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}\xi^i\cap\pi^*\alpha_i,$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups. More precisely,
$\pi_*(\xi^s\cap\pi^*\alpha)=0$ for $s<r-1$ and
$\pi_*(\xi^{r-1}\cap\pi^*\alpha)=\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in A_*(X)$
([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]).

No smoothness of $X$ is assumed; if $X$ is smooth equidimensional of dimension
$n$ then $\mathbb P(\mathcal E)$ is smooth equidimensional and the formula is a
statement about the codimension-graded Chow groups $A^*(X)$,
$A^*(\mathbb P(\mathcal E))$.
items.strategy: Stacks42.36.1-36.2, full proof locators; final certification remains owner-held. For $\alpha=[V]$, choose $r-1$ independent sections in a trivialization over its generic point: successive hyperplanes leave a section, whose pushforward is $[V]$. Each smaller hyperplane power has positive-dimensional fibres and pushes to zero. Any difference from choosing the generic trivialization is supported on a smaller closed subset, and induction plus the $c_1$ projection formula proves these identities globally. For injectivity of the displayed map push down to get $\alpha_{r-1}=0$, then multiply by $\xi$ and push to get $\alpha_{r-2}=0$, continuing down to $\alpha_0$. For surjectivity, reduce to integral $X$ by pushforward from its components. Trivialize $E$ on a dense open $U$. For $U\times\mathbb P^{r-1}$, stratify projective space into affine spaces; localization and affine homotopy invariance give generators $[\mathbb P^j]$ pulled from classes of $U$. Each generator is a hyperplane power times $\pi^*$ by repeated Cartier cutting, so the displayed map is surjective over $U$. Lift its coefficients to $X$ by localization. The residual class is supported over $X\setminus U$; induction on the dimension of the integral image proves surjectivity there, and push-pull brings it to $X$. This argument is valid without a Chow ring on $X$: $\xi$ is a first Chern cap operator and the displayed direct-sum map is an isomorphism of groups, not a module over an undefined ring.

items.title: Bivariant Chow operations
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
proper/quasi-finite and scheme base-change suppliers. Fix a field $k$ and
work in the category of schemes locally of finite type over $k$, with
$k$-morphisms. For $f:Z\to T$ in this category, a degree-$d$ bivariant
Chow operation assigns to every $k$-morphism $T'\to T$ in this category homomorphisms $c:A_m(T')\to A_{m-d}(Z\times_TT')$, commuting with
proper pushforward, flat pullback of fixed relative dimension, and Cartier
divisor Gysin. Restriction along any base morphism, composition, and proper
pushforward of such operations are defined by their action. Flat pullback and
Cartier divisor Gysin give bivariant classes. If $h:Z\to Z_1$ is proper over
$T$, pushing a class for $Z\to T$ along $h$ gives a class for $Z_1\to T$;
ordinary proper pushforward is a covariant Chow operation, not a class reversing
that proper morphism. Equality can be tested on fundamental classes of integral
schemes over $T$; it suffices to test after a proper birational modification of
each such integral scheme.

**Well-definedness.** The three axioms are required for every base change
$T'\to T$ in this category, and the operations are compared only on Chow
groups, using [[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]]. Proper
pushforward and flat pullback are the maps of
[[lem-pushforward-pullback-compatibility-chow]]; the Cartier divisor Gysin is
the operation of [[def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class]].
Restriction along a base morphism $T''\to T'$ simply changes the indexing family,
and composition of operations is associative because each axiom is applied first
to the inner and then to the outer factor; the compatibility of two Cartier
Gysins is the tame-symbol reciprocity computation of
[[lem-two-dimensional-tame-symbol-reciprocity]], and if a cycle is contained in
one of the two divisors the operation is $c_1$ of the corresponding invertible
sheaf, whose commutation is the same rational-section argument. For a proper
$h:Z\to Z_1$ over $T$ the definition $(h_*c)_{T'}=h_{T',*}c_{T'}$ satisfies the
three axioms by the corresponding compatibilities of proper pushforward with
flat pullback and Cartier Gysin. For the equality criterion, a finite cycle is
a finite sum of pushforwards of integral fundamental classes. For a locally
finite cycle $\sum_i n_i[V_i]$ on $T'$, the map
$h:\coprod_i V_i\to T'$ is proper: over every quasi-compact open only
finitely many supports occur, and their inclusions are closed immersions.
Locally finite Chow groups on this disjoint union are the product of the Chow
groups of its components, as are those of its base change to $Z$. Flat
restriction to each open-and-closed component therefore determines an
operation on the class $(n_i[V_i])_i$. Equality on the integral classes gives
equality there, and proper compatibility pushes it along $h$ to equality on
the original cycle. Finally, for a proper birational $h:V'\to V$ of integral
schemes one has $h_*[V']=[V]$, so equality on $[V']$ pushes forward to equality
on $[V]$. This is a descent test
for operations, not an assertion that Chow pullback to a modification is
injective.
items.strategy: Source: Stacks 42.29-42.35. Composition commutes with each of the three operations by applying the relevant axiom first to its inner and then its outer factor; restriction merely changes the indexing family. For a class $c$ for $Z\to T$ and a proper $h:Z\to Z_1$ over $T$, define $(h_*c)_{T\prime}=h_{T\prime,*}c_{T\prime}$. Proper composition, flat push-pull, and Cartier proper compatibility verify its three axioms. This is proper pushforward of a class, not an operation sending cycles on $T$ backwards along an arbitrary proper map. Flat pullback does so by flat composition and cartesian push-pull. For divisor Gysin, proper/flat compatibility is checked on integral cycles using the order/length definition when the cycle is not contained in the divisor, and $c_1(L)$ when it is; two Cartier Gysins commute. To verify the last assertion, when neither divisor contains the cycle their two cuts agree away from their common codimension-two locus, and the discrepancy at that locus is the principal-divisor boundary of the tame symbol $(-1)^{\operatorname{ord}a\operatorname{ord}b}a^{\operatorname{ord}b}/b^{\operatorname{ord}a}$; the two-dimensional tame-symbol reciprocity lemma proves its divisor zero in the Chow quotient. When a cycle is contained in one divisor, the operation is $c_1$ of that line bundle and commutation reduces to commutation of two first Chern operations, proved by the same rational-section argument. This supplies the Cartier axiom without higher Gysin. For the equality criterion, every finite cycle is a finite sum of pushforwards of integral fundamental classes; commute $c$ with these pushforwards. If $h:V'\to V$ is proper birational and integral, $h_*[V']=[V]$, so equality on $[V']$ pushes to equality on $[V]$. This is a descent test for operations, not an assertion that Chow pullback to the modification is injective.

items.title: Operational Chern classes, Whitney formula and regular sections
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
proper/quasi-finite and scheme base-change suppliers. Fix a field $k$ and
work with schemes locally of finite type over $k$ and $k$-morphisms. Every rank-$r$ vector
bundle $E$ on such a scheme $T$ has operators
$c_j(E):A_m(T')\to A_{m-j}(T')$ for every $T'\to T$, defined by the projective
bundle relation and commuting with the bivariant operations. They satisfy
$c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, $c(L)=1+c_1(L)$, arbitrary base restriction,
$c(E)=c(E')c(E'')$ for $0\to E'\to E\to E''\to0$, and a splitting principle by
iterated projective bundles whose flat pullback is injective after every base
change. If a section of $E$ on a pure $n$ dimensional scheme $T$ has zero scheme
regularly embedded of codimension $r$, then $c_r(E)\cap[T]=[Z(s)]$ in
$A_{n-r}(T)$. These are operators on singular schemes; a Chow ring is not
required.
items.strategy:
Sources: Stacks 42.37-42.44. For every base $T'$ and cycle $\alpha$, use the unique projective bundle expansion to define $c_j(E)\cap\alpha$ by $\sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^j\xi^{r-j}\cap\pi^*(c_j(E)\cap\alpha)=0$. All terms have the same dimension; uniqueness follows from the basis and existence by expanding $\xi^r\pi^*\alpha$. Commuting any proper, flat or divisor operation through this equation and cancelling the basis proves the corresponding compatibility. More generally for any bivariant operation $b$ the projective bundle square and $b\xi=\xi b$ give $b c_j(E)=c_j(E)b$. A line bundle gives $\xi=c_1(L)$.
For Whitney, first if $0\to1\to E\to F\to0$, $\mathbb P(F)\subset\mathbb P(E)$ is the divisor of the induced section of $\mathcal O(1)$. Push its defining degree-$r-1$ relation to $\mathbb P(E)$: this gives the degree-$r$ relation with coefficients $c_j(F)$ and last coefficient zero. Uniqueness gives $c(E)=c(F)$. For a line subbundle $L$, twist by $L^{-1}$. The identity $\mathbb P(E\otimes L^{-1})=\mathbb P(E)$ shifts $\xi$ to $\xi-c_1(L)$; expanding its powers by the binomial formula transforms the relations into $c_j(E)=c_j(F)+c_1(L)c_{j-1}(F)$. In detail, the twist relation in degree $i$ is
$$\sum_{j=0}^i(-1)^j\binom{r-i+j}{j}c_{i-j}(E)x^j=\sum_{j=0}^i(-1)^j\binom{r-1-i+j}{j}c_{i-j}(F)x^j,$$
where $x=c_1(L)$. Substitute $c_{i-j}(E)=c_{i-j}(F)+x c_{i-j-1}(F)$. Shifting the second sum's index and using $\binom{a}{j}-\binom{a-1}{j-1}=\binom{a-1}{j}$ gives exactly the right-hand side. Inductively all lower $c_{i-j}(E)$ are known and the coefficient of the only new unknown $c_i(E)$ is one, so the solution is unique. This fills the calculation omitted in Stacks40.2. For higher-rank subbundle $E'$, pull to $\mathbb P(E')$ with kernel $H$ and line quotient $L$; set $Q=\pi^*E/H$, which is an extension of $\pi^*E''$ by $L$. Induction gives $c(\pi^*E)=c(H)c(Q)=c(H)c(L)c(\pi^*E'')=c(\pi^*E')c(\pi^*E'')$; injectivity of projective bundle pullback descends the identity. Iterating kernels yields filtrations by lines; this construction applies to a finite family simultaneously and remains injective after any base change. This proves the splitting principle after Whitney, with no circular deduction from a filtration whose additivity has not yet been proved.
For the section formula use induction on $r$, the Cartier case being $r=1$. On $\mathbb P(E)$ let $t$ be the image of $s$ in $\mathcal O(1)$ and $H$ the kernel of $\pi^*E\to\mathcal O(1)$. On $Z(t)$ the section lifts to $H$ with zero scheme $\pi^{-1}Z(s)$. At its generic points the original regular sequence is transformed by an invertible change of generators to $t$ and $r-1$ generators, so they remain regular. The divisor $Z(t)$ has dimension $n+r-2$ and is generically Cartier: away from a whole projective fibre its equation is a nonzero linear polynomial; a whole fibre could be generic in this dimension only over a point of $Z(s)$ of dimension $n-1$, impossible since $\dim Z(s)=n-r$ and $r>1$. Thus the Cartier section formula and induction give $c_r(\pi^*E)[\mathbb P(E)]=c_{r-1}(H)[Z(t)]=[\pi^{-1}Z(s)]$. Injective $\pi^*$ gives the result.

items.title: Homotopy invariance for a vector bundle
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
proper/quasi-finite and scheme base-change suppliers. Fix a field $k$ and
let $T$ be locally of finite type over $k$. For any rank-$r$ vector bundle $p:E\to T$, flat pullback $p^*:A_m(T)\to A_{m+r}(E)$ is bijective,
including after every $k$-base change $T'\to T$ with $T'$ locally of finite
type over $k$. Its inverse is denoted $s_E^!$.
items.strategy: Stacks 42.36.3. Compactify $E$ using the quotient-convention bundle $q:\mathbb P(E^\vee\oplus1)\to T$. The infinity divisor is $j:\mathbb P(E^\vee)\to\mathbb P(E^\vee\oplus1)$, with divisor class $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ from the trivial summand; its complement is $E$. Localization gives $A_*(\mathbb P(E^\vee))\xrightarrow{j_*}A_*(\mathbb P(E^\vee\oplus1))\to A_*(E)\to0$. The projective bundle basis on the source has $1,\xi,\ldots,\xi^{r-1}$, and on the target $1,\xi,\ldots,\xi^r$. Cartier cutting gives $j_*\pi^*\alpha=\xi q^*\alpha$ for every cycle (both sides are the zero of the trivial-summand section on the pulled-back cycle). By the $c_1$ projection formula, $j_*(\xi^a\pi^*\alpha)=\xi^{a+1}q^*\alpha$. Therefore the image of $j_*$ is precisely the positive-$\xi$ summands, leaving the $q^*$ summand as quotient. Restriction of $q^*$ is $p^*$, proving the isomorphism and its grading. This computation applies verbatim after any base change, since both bundles and their bases pull back.

items.title: Koszul resolutions and restriction to deformation fibres
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. A section $s$ of a rank-$d$
bundle $Q$ is a **regular section** here if, at each point of its zero scheme
$Z(s)$, some local frame expresses $s$ by $d$ components forming a regular
sequence of length $d$ in the local ring. Under this hypothesis it has exact
Koszul resolution
$\bigwedge^dQ^\vee\to\cdots\to Q^\vee\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_{Z(s)}\to0$.
Tensoring with a vector bundle preserves it. If a coherent sheaf $H$ has a
finite locally free resolution on a scheme and $t$ is a Cartier equation acting
injectively on $H$, restricting the resolution to $t=0$ remains exact and
resolves $H/tH$. In the deformation blowup for a closed embedding of smooth
quasi-projective varieties $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$, let $E$ be a finite
locally free sheaf on $X$. The strict transform
$F:X\times\mathbb P^1\hookrightarrow M$ is disjoint from
$B=\operatorname{Bl}_XY$, and a resolution of $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$
restricts exactly to the ordinary $Y$ fibre and to
$P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(N\oplus1)$; on $B$ it is an exact complex.
items.strategy:
The section hypothesis requires its actual rank-d tuple to be regular of length d at each zero point. For d=0 the Koszul complex is the coefficient module in degree zero. Outside Z(s), a unit component a_j gives the contraction h(v)=a_j^-1 e_j wedge v; hence the zero-sheaf resolution is exact there. Koszul exactness follows by induction on the regular sequence: the complex on $(a_1,\ldots,a_d)$ is the mapping cone of multiplication by $a_d$ on the complex on $(a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1})$. Its long exact homology sequence leaves only degree zero because $a_d$ is injective on $A/(a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1})$, with quotient $A/(a_1,\ldots,a_d)$. Exterior powers and contraction by $s$ are canonical under change of local frames, so these local resolutions glue. For fibre restriction, the two-term free resolution $[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{t}\mathcal O]$ of $\mathcal O/(t)$ shows that $\operatorname{Tor}_1(H,\mathcal O/(t))=\ker(t:H\to H)=0$ and all higher Tors vanish. Therefore derived tensor of any locally free resolution has homology only $H/tH$, proving ordinary restriction is exact. One must check $H$, not merely the ambient scheme, is flat or $t$-torsion-free.
For the smooth deformation, étale locally on $Y$, the embedding is given by coordinate regular sequence $a_1,\ldots,a_d$. The blowup charts of $(a_1,\ldots,a_d,t)$ are smooth: the $t$-chart has coordinates $u_j=a_j/t,t$ plus coordinates on $X$, and the $a_j$-charts have the ratios $a_l/a_j,t/a_j$ plus $a_j$ and the remaining smooth coordinates. This follows by base change from the corresponding affine-space charts, using the local smooth conormal sequence to choose étale coordinates. Thus $M$ is smooth, quasi-projective and has finite locally free coherent resolutions by the named K-theory supplier. The strict transform of $X\times\mathbb P^1$ is isomorphic to that scheme (its centre is its Cartier infinity divisor); at infinity it lies entirely in the $t$-chart, at $u_1=\cdots=u_d=0$. It meets $P$ at the section $[0:1]$ and misses $B$, which meets $P$ in $\mathbb P(N)$. On this chart $P$ has equation $t$, which acts injectively on $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$ since that sheaf is the vector bundle on $X\times\mathbb P^1$. The ordinary fibre equation is likewise injective. The restriction lemma proves exactness on $P$ and on $Y$. Since the sheaf is zero near $B$, its resolution restricts to an exact complex there: locally an exact bounded complex of vector bundles resolving zero is split exact, by induction starting at its last cokernel. These calculations fill the flatness and component restriction omissions in Vakil19.

items.title: Zero-section Gysin and the excess vector subbundle formula
items.statement:
All schemes and base changes below are locally of finite type over a fixed
field $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
proper/quasi-finite and scheme base-change suppliers. For a rank-$r$ vector
bundle $p:N\to T$, let $s_N^!=(p^*)^{-1}$. If $0\to N'\to N\to Q\to0$ is exact
and $a:N'\hookrightarrow N$ is the vector subbundle immersion, then
$s_N^!a_*p'^*\alpha=c_{\operatorname{rank}Q}(Q)\cap\alpha$. In particular
$s_N^!s_*\alpha=c_r(N)\cap\alpha$. These identities and proper/flat/divisor
compatibility hold after every base change.
items.strategy: Sources: Stacks 42.44.2 and 42.36.3. Proper, flat and divisor compatibility of $s_N^!$ follows by applying the bijection $p^*$ and the corresponding push-pull or Cartier identity to each desired equality. The universal section of $p^*Q$ on $N$ is the image of its vector coordinate under $N\to Q$; its zero scheme is $N'$. For every integral $V\subset T$, its inverse image in $N$ is integral; this section cuts a polynomial regular sequence of $\operatorname{rank}Q$ fibre coordinates after a local splitting of the bundle sequence, so the regular-section formula gives $a_*p'^*[V]=c_{\operatorname{rank}Q}(p^*Q)p^*[V]=p^*(c_{\operatorname{rank}Q}(Q)[V])$. Linearity and bijective $p^*$ prove the displayed equality. Put $N'=0$ to obtain the zero-section/self-intersection formula. All splittings here are local and used to verify regularity only, not to assert a global bundle splitting.

items.title: K-theory generators for a relative projective bundle
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. Let $Y$ be smooth
quasi-projective over a field and $E$ a rank-$r$ bundle. For
$q:P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(E)\to Y$, $K^0(P)=G_0(P)$ is generated as a
$K^0(Y)$-module by $\mathcal O(a)$, $0\le a<r$. For $r\ge1$ and $a\ge0$,
$q_!\mathcal O(a)=\operatorname{Sym}^a(E^\vee)$. For $r=0$, the projective
bundle is empty, its $K$-groups and all $q_!\mathcal O(a)$ are zero, and the
assertion of generation is vacuous. This statement has the
corresponding dual form for quotient projective bundles.
items.strategy: Use the relative diagonal in $P\times_YP$. Let $L_1=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal O(-1)$ and $Q_2$ the pullback of the tautological quotient of $q^*E$. The diagonal is the zero scheme of $L_1\to Q_2$, a regular section of $L_1^\vee\otimes Q_2$ of rank $r-1$: in matching affine charts its actual section components are $u_i-v_i$ in $A[u,v]$. Successive elimination makes each next component monic in a new variable, hence regular over every base ring and after arbitrary base change. For $r=1$ the tuple is empty; off the diagonal a component is a unit locally. Its exact Koszul resolution has terms $\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal O(-j)\otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*\bigwedge^jQ^\vee$. For a vector bundle $H$ on $P$, tensor the resolution with $\operatorname{pr}_1^*H$ and push by $\operatorname{pr}_2$. The diagonal term pushes to $H$, so the K projection formula and flat base change for $q$ give $[H]=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}(-1)^j q^*(q_!(H(-j)))\,[\bigwedge^jQ^\vee]$. Base change here is the product projective-bundle square and can be verified on the standard projective affine cover: its Čech complexes tensor along the flat bundle projection, so their cohomology classes agree. From $0\to Q^\vee\to q^*E^\vee\to\mathcal O(1)\to0$, the exterior filtration identity gives $[\bigwedge^jQ^\vee]=\sum_{a=0}^j(-1)^a q^*[\bigwedge^{j-a}E^\vee][\mathcal O(a)]$. Thus each diagonal resolution term lies in the span of $\mathcal O(0),\ldots,\mathcal O(r-1)$, proving generation. Coherent sheaves reduce to vector bundles by finite resolution on the smooth quasi-projective $P$. For $a\ge0$, the local projective-space cohomology calculation has only degree-zero cohomology with its homogeneous monomial basis; changes of trivialization act by $\operatorname{Sym}^a(E^\vee)$, proving the pushforward formula globally, with higher direct images zero. This argument is a local completion of the general-bundle extension mentioned in the original scaffold; it uses no Riemann-Roch theorem.

items.title: Specialization as a bivariant operation and base change
items.statement:
All schemes and base changes below are locally of finite type over a fixed
field $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
smooth-immersion and homological suppliers. For a closed immersion
$Z\hookrightarrow T$ with a surjection $N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$
from a rank-$d$ bundle on $Z$, each $T'\to T$ gives $Z'=Z\times_TT'$, a closed
cone embedding $a:C_{Z'}T'\hookrightarrow N'=N|_{Z'}$, and an operation
$c(Z,T,N):=(p'^*)^{-1}a_*\sigma_{Z'/T'}:A_m(T')\to A_{m-d}(Z')$. This family is
bivariant and compatible with arbitrary base restriction. If
$N'_{0}\subset N'$ is a vector subbundle through which the cone embedding
factors, the operation defined with $N'$ is the operation defined with
$N'_{0}$ followed by the top Chern operator of $N'/N'_{0}$:
$c(Z',T',N')=c_{d-d_0}(N'/N'_0)\cap c(Z',T',N'_0)$, where
$d_0=\operatorname{rank}N'_0$.
items.strategy: Sources: Stacks 42.48.1-48.3 and 42.54.1-54.5, full text retrieved; final source-to-argument certification remains owner-held. The ideal generating $Z'$ is $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$, so its powers are generated by the images of powers of $\mathcal I$; hence $\operatorname{Sym}(N'^\vee)\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}}\mathcal O_{T'}$. This proves the cone embedding for arbitrary, including nonflat, base change. For a proper $W\to\mathbb P^1_T$ isomorphic over $\mathbb A^1_T$, define infinity specialization on each base by lifting $\mathbb A^1$ pullback and applying Cartier Gysin at infinity. Localization and the trivial fibre normal line make the lift irrelevant. To commute it with a proper map, push forward any lift; its restriction is the proper push of the original pullback, and Cartier Gysin commutes with pushforward. To commute with flat pullback, pull back the lift and use flat/Cartier compatibility. To commute with a Cartier divisor Gysin, apply that Gysin to the lift and use commutation of Cartier Gysins; its ordinary restriction is the lift of the desired input. These arguments prove each bivariant axiom without an unspecified diagram chase. If a proper $W_1\to W_2$ is an isomorphism over the ordinary part, pushing a lift from $W_1$ to $W_2$ proves equality of their infinity operations after pushforward. Under nonflat base change, the blowup of $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$ has a closed immersion into the base change of the original blowup, induced by the surjection of Rees algebras, and is an isomorphism over the ordinary part. The preceding proper comparison therefore shows that the cone portions give the same class after pushforward to $N'$. Proper pushforward, open restriction and $(p'^*)^{-1}$ are bivariant, proving the claim. If the cone factors through $N'_0$, apply the vector subbundle identity of [[lem-zero-section-gysin-and-excess-vector-subbundle]] to its specialization class (write that class as $p_0^*\beta$ by homotopy invariance). This gives the excess factor exactly.

items.title: Commutation and composition of refined Gysin operations
items.statement:
All schemes and base changes below are locally of finite type over a fixed
field $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the smooth
normal-sequence suppliers. The operations $c(Z,T,N)$ of
[[lem-gysin-specialization-bivariant-and-base-change]] commute with every
bivariant operation. Given $Z\subset Y\subset T$ and virtual normal bundles
fitting into $0\to N_{Z/Y}\to N_{Z/T}\to N_{Y/T}|_Z\to0$ compatible with the
conormal maps, $c(Z,T,N_{Z/T})=c(Z,Y,N_{Z/Y})c(Y,T,N_{Y/T})$. For regular
embeddings this yields $(j i)^!=i^!j^!$, after all base changes. If a regular
embedding is followed by a smooth projection, its Gysin likewise composes with
the projection pullback; in particular a regular section of a smooth morphism
gives $s^!p^*=1$.
items.strategy:
Sources: Stacks 42.54.8-54.10 and 42.59.1-59.6. Test equality on integral $T'\to T$, allowing proper birational modification by the bivariant criterion. If its inverse image of $Z$ is all of $T'$, the cone is the zero section and $c$ is the top Chern operator by [[lem-zero-section-gysin-and-excess-vector-subbundle]], hence central. Otherwise blow up the nonzero ideal of the inverse image of $Z$. The new inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor; the pulled-back virtual normal bundle surjects onto its normal line and the kernel is a vector bundle $Q$ (dually the conormal surjection has locally free kernel). The excess formula gives $c=c_{\mathrm{top}}(Q)D^!$. Both factors commute with every bivariant operation, respectively by [[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]] and the Cartier axiom. Proper pushforward of the fundamental class proves commutation on the original integral base. Thus no unproved Gysin commutation is used.
For composition, use the same equality criterion and blow up the product of the two nonzero ideals to make both inverse images Cartier; invertibility of a product ideal implies invertibility of its factors locally on this blowup, since each factor generates an invertible fractional ideal. If an inverse image is the entire base, the identity reduces directly to the excess vector subbundle formula. In the Cartier case split off the excess bundle for $Y/T$ using the two exact sequences. Centrality of its top Chern operation reduces the question to the case that $N_{Y/T}$ is the normal line to $Y$ in $T$. Denote its zero section by $o:Y\to C_YT$. The essential cone identity is $o^![C_ZT]=[C_ZY]$ as a class in $A_{n-1}(C_ZT\times_{C_YT}Y)$ for integral $T$ of dimension $n$. Here is the full local calculation omitted in Stacks54.9. On an affine open of the integral ambient scheme write $Z=(a)$ and $Y=(b)$, with $b=ac$ and $a,b\ne0$. Their open deformation rings are
$$R_a=A[t,u]/(tu-a)=A[t,a/t],\qquad R_b=A[t,v]/(tv-b)=A[t,b/t].$$
Both inject into $A[t,t^{-1}]$, since their principal ideals are generated by nonzerodivisors. The homomorphism $R_b\to R_a$ sends $v\mapsto cu$. It defines a morphism from the whole $t$-chart of the $Z$ blowup to the $t$-chart of the $Y$ blowup; on $t=0$ it is exactly the map of normal cones induced by the inclusion of ideals. Together with the ordinary part these charts give the open $U$ needed in Stacks54.9, containing the whole $C_ZT$.
The strict transform of $Y\times\mathbb P^1$ in the $Z$ blowup has, on this chart, coordinate ring
$$R_a/((b)R_a:t^\infty)=(A/(b))[t,\bar a/t]\subset(A/(b))[t,t^{-1}].$$
Indeed the kernel of the displayed map from $R_a$ is its contraction of $(b)$ after inverting $t$, which is precisely that saturation. The special fibre is $\operatorname{gr}_{(\bar a)}(A/(b))$, proving that its cone part is $C_ZY$ with every nonreduced multiplicity. Saturation is essential: when $b=a^2$, the quotient has relation $u^2=0$ at infinity, rather than the erroneous relation $\bar c u=0$ alone.
The strict transform $\mathbb P^1_Y$ in the $Y$ blowup is the Cartier divisor $v=0$ in its $t$-chart; its infinity restriction is the zero section $o:Y\to C_YT$. Pulling back its Cartier operator to $U$ cuts by $cu$ on the total space, an actual nonzero divisor because $R_a$ is a domain. On the ordinary part this agrees with the strict transform just computed, so their Cartier cycle classes differ by classes supported at infinity. Infinity Cartier Gysin kills every such difference: its normal line is trivial, and $j^!j_*\eta=c_1(1)\eta=0$. Cartier commutation therefore gives
$$o^![C_ZT]=j_\infty^!v^![U]=j_\infty^![\widetilde Y]=[C_ZY]$$
in the actual fibre product $C_ZT\times_{C_YT}Y$. This does not assume $cu$ remains a regular equation after setting $t=0$; the middle calculation is on the total deformation, and the Cartier operation includes its contained-component case. In the vector-bundle square $N_{Z/Y}\subset N_{Z/T}\to N_{Y/T}|_Z$, Cartier Gysin for the kernel commutes with bundle pullback and sends the first cone class to the second by this identity. Apply the two inverse bundle pullbacks: they characterize precisely the two sides of the composition formula, so they agree. Push down the modifications to finish.
Finally suppose $s:Z\hookrightarrow P$ is a regular immersion, $P\to T$ is smooth and $Z\to T$ is flat of the expected relative dimension. Its equations remain regular after every base change on $T$. To prove this locally, write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $P=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}C$. The Koszul resolution of $C$ over $B$ has $A$-flat terms because $B$ is smooth and therefore flat over $A$, and its quotient $C$ is $A$-flat by hypothesis. Successive short exact kernel sequences show every kernel is $A$-flat: tensor exactness follows from $\operatorname{Tor}_1$ of the flat quotient being zero, and higher Tor vanishing gives flatness of the kernel. Tensoring this resolution with any $A'$ therefore remains exact. Localizing gives regular equations on $B\otimes_AA'$ (Koszul exactness for a finite sequence in a Noetherian local maximal ideal implies regularity, by induction using the last-variable mapping cone and Nakayama). Thus its normal cone is the full base-changed normal bundle, with fundamental cycle equal to bundle pullback of $[Z\times_TV]$ for each integral $V\to T$. Inverting bundle pullback gives $s^!p^*=(ps)^*$. The section case has $ps=1$, so $s^!p^*=1$.
For composition of graph pullbacks of $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to W$ between smooth schemes, work in $X\times Y\times W$. The two pulled-back graphs intersect in the graph of $(f,gf)$; their equations form regular sequences with independent $Y$ and $W$ coordinate directions. Regular-immersion composition and bivariant commutation identify the iterated operation with the small graph Gysin followed by pullback from $W$. To compare with the graph of $gf$ in $X\times W$, project away $Y$. The embedding $X\times W\to X\times Y\times W$ given by $(x,w)\mapsto(x,f(x),w)$ is a regular section of this smooth projection. Its Gysin cancels projection pullback by the section identity just proved; regular-immersion composition then reduces the small graph operation to the graph of $gf$. This proves graph composition and independence of graph presentations without an unproved local flatness criterion. All normal-bundle equalities used in this argument are exact sequences, not global splittings.

items.title: Refined Gysin pullback for a regular embedding of smooth schemes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the smooth
normal-sequence suppliers. Fix a field $k$; all schemes and base changes below
are locally of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms. Let $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be a regular closed
embedding of codimension $d$ with normal bundle $N$. In particular a closed
embedding of smooth schemes of constant codimension is regular. For any
$f:Y'\to Y$, put $X'=X\times_YY'$ and $N'=N|_{X'}$. The pulled-back ideal gives
a closed immersion $a:C_{X'}Y'\hookrightarrow N'$. Define
$$i^!_{Y'}=(p'^*)^{-1}a_*\sigma_{X'/Y'}:A_m(Y')\longrightarrow A_{m-d}(X'),$$
using [[def-deformation-to-the-normal-cone-and-specialization]] and
[[lem-vector-bundle-chow-homotopy-invariance]]. No fibre product of deformation
spaces over $\mathbb P^1$ with a fictitious map to $Y$ is used. The same
construction for a regular locally closed embedding uses restriction to an open
in which it is closed; the operations agree under further restriction and
extension of cycles, so this is intrinsic.

For $h:Y''\to Y'$ and $h_X:X''=X\times_YY''\to X'$, properness of $h$ gives
$i^!_{Y'}h_*=(h_X)_*i^!_{Y''}$, and flatness of $h$ of fixed pure relative dimension gives
$i^!_{Y''}h^*=h_X^*i^!_{Y'}$. These do not require the base-changed embedding to
be regular. If $X'\hookrightarrow Y'$ is regular with normal bundle
$N_0\subset N'$ and excess bundle $Q=N'/N_0$, then
$i^!_{Y'}=c_{d-\operatorname{rank}N_0}(Q)\cap (i')^!$. In particular
$i^!i_*\alpha=c_d(N)\cap\alpha$. Here $c_j$ means the already defined
operational Chern operator of
[[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]]; it later becomes the
Chow-ring Chern class on a smooth scheme. Codimension-one Gysin equals Cartier
divisor Gysin; refined Gysins commute, and $(ji)^!=i^!j^!$ for composed regular
embeddings. They commute with Chern cap operations. For any operational class
$c$ on $Y$ and $\beta\in A_*(X)$, its projection formula is
$i_*(c|_X\cap\beta)=c\cap i_*\beta$. Under the later smooth operational-ring
identification this is the ring formula
$i_*(i^*\alpha\cdot\beta)=\alpha\cdot i_*\beta$.

**Well-definedness.** The construction and the arbitrary-base-change bivariant
axioms are proved in
[[lem-gysin-specialization-bivariant-and-base-change]]: the specialization
$\sigma_{X'/Y'}$ is well defined on Chow groups by the triviality of the normal
line at infinity, the cone embedding exists by the Rees-algebra surjection, and
$a_*$ and $(p'^*)^{-1}$ are the proper pushforward and inverse flat pullback of
[[lem-vector-bundle-chow-homotopy-invariance]]. The excess formula is the
corresponding statement of [[lem-gysin-specialization-bivariant-and-base-change]];
for the self-intersection formula apply it to the base change $Y'=X$, where the
ideal is zero, the cone is the zero section and the quotient bundle is $N$, and
use proper compatibility to identify the restricted operation with $i^!i_*$. For
the agreement with Cartier divisor Gysin in codimension one, test on an integral
base cycle: if the cycle is not contained in the divisor its cone is the normal
line and the operation is its Cartier fundamental cycle, while if it is
contained the zero-cone computation gives $c_1$ of the restricted normal line,
which are exactly the two cases of the Cartier Gysin of
[[def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class]]. Commutation
and composition, including the necessary cone computation with the saturated
strict transforms in the deformation charts, are
[[lem-refined-gysin-commutation-and-composition]]. Locality for locally closed
embeddings follows because on each cycle the identical ideal and normal bundle
give identical operators, and in overlaps the two restrictions agree. The
operational projection formula is the proper axiom of a bivariant class
([[lem-refined-gysin-commutation-and-composition]]); its ring interpretation is
provided by the later smooth-ring theorem and is not a prerequisite for this
construction.
items.strategy:
The construction and arbitrary-base-change bivariant axioms are proved in [[lem-gysin-specialization-bivariant-and-base-change]], with its excess vector subbundle formula. Self-intersection applies that formula to the base change $Y'=X$: the ideal is zero, its cone is the zero section, and the quotient bundle is $N$; use proper compatibility to identify this restricted operation with $i^!i_*$. For Cartier agreement, test on an integral base cycle. If it is not contained in the divisor, its cone is the normal line and the operation is its Cartier fundamental cycle; if contained, the zero-cone computation gives $c_1$ of the restricted normal line. These are exactly the two cases of Cartier Gysin. Commutation and composition, including the necessary cone calculation, are [[lem-refined-gysin-commutation-and-composition]]. Locality for locally closed embeddings follows from the same cone formula on every cycle and independence of a lift in specialization; in each overlap the identical ideal and normal bundle give identical operators. The operational projection formula is the proper axiom of a bivariant class; its ring interpretation is provided by the later smooth-ring theorem, and is not a prerequisite for this construction. Source route is Stacks42.48/53/54/59 with the exact local helpers above. Vakil16-17 supply construction and statements, but their omitted proofs do not establish these properties; Fulton has not been read and is not a proof premise.

items.title: The intersection product and Chow ring of a smooth scheme
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
smooth-immersion and homological suppliers. For a smooth equidimensional finite
type $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $n$, $A^p(X)=A_{n-p}(X)$ is a commutative
graded ring with unit $[X]$ and product
$\alpha\beta=\Delta_X^!(\alpha\times\beta)$. The diagonal is a regular immersion
(closed if $X$ is separated); use the locally closed extension of
[[def-refined-gysin-pullback-for-regular-embeddings]] otherwise. Exterior
product on integral cycles is the fundamental cycle $[V\times_k W]$, with
generic lengths and all components; over a non-algebraically-closed field this
product scheme need not be integral. Exterior product descends to rational
equivalence and is associative and symmetric. Every morphism $f:X'\to X$ of
smooth finite type $k$-schemes has a codimension-preserving ring pullback
$f^*:=\Gamma_f^!\operatorname{pr}_X^*$; it agrees with flat pullback when $f$ is
flat and obeys composition. If $X'$ has open equidimensional components
$X'_j$ of dimensions $n_j$, set $A^p(X'):=\bigoplus_j A_{n_j-p}(X'_j)$,
with componentwise product. For proper $f$, the restriction $f_j:X'_j\to X$
has $f_{j,*}:A^p(X'_j)\to A^{p+n-n_j}(X)$, and
$f_*(f^*\alpha\,\beta)=\alpha f_*\beta$ in the total Chow group.
Thus the single shift $n-\dim X'$ applies when $X'$ is equidimensional. Operational $c_j(E)$ correspond to
classes $c_j(E)\cap[X]$ and their cap action is multiplication by these classes;
in particular $c_1(L)\alpha=c_1(L)\cap\alpha$. More generally the operational
action on $A_*(X)$ agrees with the product after the dimension identification.
items.strategy:
Sources: Stacks42.60-42.62. Fix integral $V\subset X$. Its exterior-product operation is proper pushforward of flat pullback along $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is therefore bivariant and factors through rational equivalence in the other input. Symmetry proves descent in the first input too. Associativity is checked on the fundamental cycles of triple products: the iterated flat pullbacks both give their generic lengths, by associativity of tensor products and flat length multiplicity; extension is bilinear. Such exterior-product operations commute with all bivariant operations because their two constituents do. Consequently associativity of $\Delta^!$ product follows by comparing the two embeddings $\Delta_{12},\Delta_{23}$ in $X^3$: their iterated Gysins both give the small diagonal Gysin by [[lem-refined-gysin-commutation-and-composition]], while exterior-product compatibility moves each inner Gysin into $X^3$. Symmetry of $\Delta$ gives ordinary commutativity (no cohomological sign).
For the unit, $\alpha\times[X]$ is the pullback of $\alpha$ by the smooth first projection, and $\Delta^!\operatorname{pr}_1^*=1$ by the smooth-section identity in that helper. Thus $\Delta^!(\alpha\times[X])=\alpha$ on every class, not merely on a generic open.
The full operational identification can be proved explicitly. A bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to X)$ maps to $c[X]\in A_{n-p}(X)$. Conversely $\alpha\in A_{n-p}(X)$ assigns to $T\to X$ the operation $\beta\mapsto\Delta^!(\alpha\times\beta)$ on $T$; its proper, flat and Cartier compatibility comes from exterior product and refined Gysin. This operation evaluated on $[X]$ is $\alpha$ by the unit computation. To prove the inverse in the other direction, commute $c$ past the exterior product and diagonal Gysin: $\Delta^!((c[X])\times\beta)=c\Delta^!([X]\times\beta)=c\beta$. Hence composition of operational classes is exactly the product. For a graph, its immersion is regular since it is a section of a smooth projection; the graph Gysin constructed in the helper composes, is central, sends $[X]$ to $[X']$, and agrees with flat pullback by its smooth/flat composition identity. Thus applying graph Gysin to $c[X]$ gives the restricted operation $c[X']$, proving ring naturality and the unit assertion. For proper $f$, write $\alpha=c[X]$. Then $f_*(f^*\alpha\,\beta)=f_*(c\beta)=c f_*\beta=\alpha f_*\beta$ by the proper axiom. The operational Chern identification follows from the same isomorphism. This proves every displayed operation integrally and avoids relying on the rational Chern-character isomorphism.

items.title: Naturality and projection formula for the Chow ring
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
smooth-immersion and homological suppliers. For every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of
smooth equidimensional finite type schemes over $k$, $f^*:A^*(Y)\to A^*(X)$ is
the graph Gysin pullback, preserves codimension and the unit, is a ring
homomorphism, and obeys $(gf)^*=f^*g^*$. If $f$ is flat it is precisely the
previously defined flat pullback. For proper $f$, proper pushforward shifts
codimension by $\dim Y-\dim X$, obeys $(gf)_*=g_*f_*$ for proper composites, and
$f_*(f^*\alpha\cdot\beta)=\alpha\cdot f_*\beta$. Flat/proper composition laws
are asserted under their respective hypotheses, not by identifying the two
kinds of operation.
items.strategy: Use the operational isomorphism and graph computation established in [[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]. Restriction of operational classes is a ring map and composes, so graph pullback is a unital ring map. For flat $f$, the graph's Gysin followed by the smooth projection is the flat pullback by [[lem-refined-gysin-commutation-and-composition]]. If $\alpha=c[Y]$, its pullback is $c[X]$ and the proper axiom gives $f_*(c\beta)=c f_*\beta$, the required projection formula. Proper composition is checked on each integral cycle using multiplication of generic degrees, with zero pushforward when dimension drops, and then descends to Chow groups. The degree shift follows from $A^p(X)=A_{\dim X-p}(X)$ and dimension preservation by proper pushforward of nonzero cycles. No undefined pullback for merely proper maps is used.

items.title: Chern classes of a vector bundle in the Chow ring
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
smooth-immersion and homological suppliers. Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a
smooth equidimensional scheme of finite type over $k$ of dimension $n$
([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]], [[def-relative-dimension-smooth-morphism]]),
with Chow ring $A^*(X)$
([[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]). Let $\mathcal E$
be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of rank $r\ge1$
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]), with projective bundle
$\pi:\mathbb P(\mathcal E)\to X$ and $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$
([[thm-projective-bundle-formula-for-chow-groups]]).

**Definition.** By the projective bundle formula, $\xi^r\in A^r(\mathbb P(\mathcal E))$
has a unique expression
$$\xi^r+\sum_{i=1}^{r}(-1)^i c_i(\mathcal E)\,\xi^{r-i}=0\qquad\text{in }A^*(\mathbb P(\mathcal E)),$$
with $c_i(\mathcal E)\in A^i(X)$ pulled back from $X$; the classes $c_i(\mathcal E)$
are the **Chern classes** of $\mathcal E$. Set $c_0(\mathcal E):=1\in A^0(X)$,
$c_i(\mathcal E):=0$ for $i>r$, and call
$c(\mathcal E):=1+c_1(\mathcal E)+\dots+c_r(\mathcal E)$ the **total Chern class**.

For the zero bundle define $c(0)=1$ and $c_i(0)=0$ for $i>0$, as for the rank-zero operational classes; no projective bundle of rank zero is used.

**Basic properties.** (i) (Normalization) For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$:
$c(\mathcal L)=1+c_1(\mathcal L)$ with $c_1(\mathcal L)\in A^1(X)$ the first Chern
class of [[def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class]]; in
particular $c_1(\mathcal O_X(D))=[D]$ for an effective Cartier divisor $D$.
(ii) (Naturality) For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ of smooth equidimensional
$k$-schemes, $c_i(f^*\mathcal E)=f^*c_i(\mathcal E)$. (iii) (Vanishing)
$c_i(\mathcal E)=0$ for $i>\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E$ and
$c_i(\mathcal E)\in A^i(X)$. (iv) (Direct sums of line bundles) If
$\mathcal E\cong\mathcal L_1\oplus\dots\oplus\mathcal L_r$ then
$c(\mathcal E)=\prod_{i=1}^r(1+c_1(\mathcal L_i))$. (v) (Top class)
$c_r(\mathcal E)\cap[X]=[Z(s)]$ for a regular section $s$ of $\mathcal E$ with
$\dim Z(s)=n-r$; in particular $c_r(\mathcal E)$ is the class of the zero locus
of a regular section.

**Well-definedness.** The classes are defined by applying the operational Chern
operators of [[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]] to the
fundamental class $[X]$ and using the operational-ring isomorphism of
[[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]], which identifies
the operational action with multiplication: their defining projective bundle
relation is exactly the displayed relation, and the basis part of
[[thm-projective-bundle-formula-for-chow-groups]] gives existence and uniqueness
of the coefficients. Normalization, naturality under arbitrary morphisms of
smooth schemes, rank vanishing, the Whitney and line-summand formulas and the
regular-section formula (including its generic multiplicities and the case of a
non-reduced zero scheme) are already established for the operational classes;
restriction of operational classes is the graph pullback under the operational
isomorphism, by
[[lem-chow-ring-naturality-and-projection-formula]], so they become the claimed
ring identities. Only the injectivity of projective-bundle pullback is used, not
injectivity of arbitrary $f^*$.
items.strategy: Define the classes by applying the operators of [[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]] to $[X]$ and use the operational-ring isomorphism in [[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]. Its projective bundle relation gives exactly the displayed relation and uniqueness. Normalization, arbitrary morphism naturality, rank vanishing, Whitney and the line-summand formula are already established for the operators; restriction under the operational isomorphism is the graph pullback, so these become the claimed ring identities. The regular-section formula follows from the supplier's projective-bundle induction and gives its zero-scheme fundamental cycle, with generic multiplicities. No assertion that arbitrary $f^*$ is injective is used; only flag/projective bundle pullback is injective.

items.title: Additivity, naturality and the splitting principle for Chern classes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
smooth-immersion and homological suppliers. Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a smooth
equidimensional $k$-scheme of finite type, and let
$0\to\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E''\to0$ be a short exact sequence of
finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-modules
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]). Ranks are allowed to be locally
constant: define Chern classes componentwise on the finitely many open-and-closed
rank loci, using [[def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle]] on each constant-rank locus. Then:

1. (Whitney additivity) $c(\mathcal E)=c(\mathcal E')\,c(\mathcal E'')$ in the
   Chow ring $A^*(X)$ ([[def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle]],
   [[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]).
2. (Naturality) If $f:X'\to X$ is a flat morphism of smooth equidimensional
   $k$-schemes of finite type, then $c_i(f^*\mathcal E)=f^*c_i(\mathcal E)$ for all $i$.
3. (Splitting principle) There exists a morphism $f:X'\to X$, a composition of
   projective bundles over $X$, with $X'$ smooth and equidimensional, such that
   $f^*:A^*(X)\to A^*(X')$ is injective. On each rank locus
   $X_r=\{x:\operatorname{rank}_x\mathcal E=r\}$, its inverse image admits a filtration
   $$0=\mathcal E_0\subseteq\mathcal E_1\subseteq\dots\subseteq\mathcal E_r=f^*\mathcal E$$
   with successive quotients invertible sheaves
   $\mathcal L_1,\dots,\mathcal L_r$; consequently
   $f^*c(\mathcal E)=\prod_{i=1}^r(1+c_1(\mathcal L_i))$. Any polynomial identity
   among Chern classes that is proved on every rank locus after replacing $\mathcal E$ by such a
   filtered bundle and $c_i(\mathcal E)$ by the elementary symmetric functions
   $e_i(c_1(\mathcal L_j))$ holds for $\mathcal E$ itself.
4. (Consequences) $c_i(\mathcal E^\vee)=(-1)^ic_i(\mathcal E)$;
   $c_1(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)=c_1(\mathcal L)+c_1(\mathcal M)$ for
   invertible sheaves; $c_i(\mathcal E)=0$ for
   $i>r$ on $X_r$; and for an exact sequence of vector
   bundles the total Chern classes multiply (this is (1)).
items.strategy: Apply [[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]] through the operational isomorphism of the smooth Chow ring. That supplier proves Whitney first by the line-subbundle and rank induction argument, then constructs flags by taking successive kernels of tautological line quotients, rather than assuming the kernel on $\mathbb P(E)$ is pulled from $X$. Each bundle pullback is injective by the projective bundle formula, so their composition is injective. A filtration gives the line-product formula by already proved Whitney. The dual filtration has quotients $L_j^{-1}$, whose first Chern operators are the negatives of those of $L_j$ by the rational-section divisor construction; multiplying $\prod(1-x_j)$ gives $c_i(E^\vee)=(-1)^ic_i(E)$. The tensor identity for two lines follows by taking the product of rational sections and adding their Cartier divisors. All vanishings are in the defining operator relation. This is the exact Stacks42.39-43 proof route with its local induction supplied.

items.title: Chern character and Todd class
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. Let $k$ be a field and let $X$
be a smooth equidimensional $k$-scheme of finite type
([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]), with Chow ring $A^*(X)$
([[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]) and
vector-bundle group $K^0(X)$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]).
When $X$ is additionally quasi-projective,
[[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]] identifies this group with
coherent $K_0(X)$; that extra hypothesis is required for the coherent-group
extension. Write $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}:=A^*(X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$. If $n=\dim X$,
$A^i(X)=A_{n-i}(X)=0$ for $i>n$, since there are no negative-dimensional
integral cycles. Every series below is evaluated only through degree $n$;
in particular positive-codimension elements are nilpotent. For the rank-zero
bundle the empty root list gives $\operatorname{ch}(0)=0$ and
$\operatorname{td}(0)=1$.

**Chern roots.** The **Chern roots** of a finite locally free
$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ are formal symbols
$x_1,\dots,x_r$ with the property that the elementary symmetric functions in the
$x_i$ are the Chern classes: $e_i(x_1,\dots,x_r)=c_i(\mathcal E)$
([[def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle]]); by the splitting principle every
symmetric polynomial expression in the $x_i$ with rational coefficients defines
a well-defined element of $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$
([[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]]).

**Chern character.** Define
$$\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E):=\sum_{j=1}^{r}e^{x_j}=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac{1}{m!}\,p_m(c_1,\dots,c_m)\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q},$$
where $p_0:=r=\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E$, while for $m\ge1$ the
power sum $p_m(c_1,\dots,c_m)=\sum_jx_j^m$ is a universal polynomial in
the Chern classes. Thus $\operatorname{ch}_0(\mathcal E)=r$; explicitly
$\operatorname{ch}=r+c_1+\tfrac12(c_1^2-2c_2)+\tfrac16(c_1^3-3c_1c_2+3c_3)+\cdots$
(the denominators are why we tensor with $\mathbb Q$).

**Todd class.** Define
$$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E):=\prod_{j=1}^{r}\frac{x_j}{1-e^{-x_j}}\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q};$$
explicitly
$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E)=1+\tfrac12c_1+\tfrac1{12}(c_1^2+c_2)+\tfrac1{24}c_1c_2+\cdots$.
For a smooth $X$ the **Todd class of $X$** is $\operatorname{td}(T_X)$ for the
tangent bundle $T_X=\operatorname{Hom}(\Omega^1_{X/k},\mathcal O_X)$
([[def-sheaf-relative-differentials]],
[[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]]).

**Line bundles.** For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ with
$x=c_1(\mathcal L)$: $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal L)=e^{x}$ and
$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal L)=x/(1-e^{-x})=1+\tfrac12x+\tfrac1{12}x^2-\cdots$.

**Well-definedness.** After truncation at degree $n$, the positive-degree
components of the Chern character and all components of the Todd class are
symmetric polynomials with rational coefficients in the Chern roots, hence
universal polynomial expressions in their elementary symmetric functions,
the Chern classes of [[def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle]]. The degree-zero
component of the Chern character is the rank $r$. Thus the Chern character
depends only on the rank and Chern classes of $\mathcal E$, whereas the Todd
class depends only on its Chern classes. For locally constant ranks these
formulas are interpreted componentwise on the finite open-and-closed rank
loci. By the splitting principle of
[[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]], these values are
independent of the choice of flag bundle or filtration: any two filtrations
have the same rank and elementary symmetric functions, and hence give the
same polynomial values. Rational coefficients are needed for
the exponential and geometric expansions, which is why the target is
$A^*(X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$. The tangent bundle is finite locally free
of rank $\dim X$ by [[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]], so its Chern
roots and Todd class are defined; the Todd class is multiplicative in exact sequences, whereas the Chern
character is additive, and the
identification of $K^0(X)$ with $K_0(X)$ on a quasi-projective $X$ lets the
character be evaluated on coherent classes through the finite locally free
resolutions of [[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]].
items.strategy:
Definitions via Chern roots, following Stacks, *Chow Homology*, Section 42.45 (tag 02UM, the Chern character and tensor products) and Section 42.65 (tag 02UN, Todd classes), and Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 6 (Chern classes) and 7 (the Todd class $T(X)$ of the tangent bundle, an element of $A(X)\otimes\mathbb Q$); the explicit expansions are Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 3.2.3 and Vakil 245 Class 18 Sections 2.1-2.2 (the definitions $\operatorname{ch}(E)=\sum e^{\alpha_i}$ and $\operatorname{td}(E)=\prod Q(\alpha_i)$, with $Q(x)=x/(1-e^{-x})$). Well-definedness of the Chern character in the rank and Chern classes, and of the Todd class in the Chern classes, follows from the splitting principle of [[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]]: any two filtrations with invertible quotients have the same rank and elementary symmetric functions, so the character and Todd polynomials have the same values; rational coefficients are needed for the exponential and the geometric expansions. The tangent bundle is locally free of rank $\dim X$ by [[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]].

items.title: Additivity of the Chern character and multiplicativity of the Todd class
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. In the setting of
[[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]] let
$0\to\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E''\to0$ be a short exact sequence of
finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-modules
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]). Then:

1. $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E')+\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E'')$
   in $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$; hence $\operatorname{ch}$ is additive in exact
   sequences and descends to a group homomorphism
   $$\operatorname{ch}:K^0(X)\longrightarrow A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}.$$
2. $\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E')\,\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E'')$;
   hence $\operatorname{td}$ is multiplicative in exact sequences and depends
   only on the class of $\mathcal E$ in $K^0(X)$.
3. For finite locally free $\mathcal E,\mathcal F$:
   $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal F)=\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)$,
   $\operatorname{ch}_m(\mathcal E^\vee)=(-1)^m\operatorname{ch}_m(\mathcal E)$;
   equivalently $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\vee)=\sum e^{-x_j}$ when
   $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum e^{x_j}$, and
   $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal O_X)=\operatorname{rank}=1$. Hence
   $\operatorname{ch}:K^0(X)\to A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ is a ring homomorphism with
   the vector-bundle tensor product.
4. For a flat morphism $f:X'\to X$ of smooth equidimensional $k$-schemes:
   $f^*\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{ch}(f^*\mathcal E)$ and
   $f^*\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{td}(f^*\mathcal E)$; and
   $\operatorname{td}(T_{X\times_kX'})=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\operatorname{td}(T_X)\cdot\operatorname{pr}_2^*\operatorname{td}(T_{X'})$.
5. For line bundles:
   $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal L_1\oplus\dots\oplus\mathcal L_r)=\sum e^{c_1(\mathcal L_j)}$
   and $\operatorname{td}(\mathcal L)=\tfrac{c_1(\mathcal L)}{1-e^{-c_1(\mathcal L)}}$
   (formal series); the terms of degree $>\dim X$ vanish. If $X$ is
   quasi-projective, transport these maps along the finite-resolution
   isomorphism $K^0(X)=K_0(X)$. The product on coherent $K_0$ is the transported
   vector-bundle product, equivalently the alternating Tor product; ordinary
   tensor product of two arbitrary coherent sheaves is not assumed additive in
   exact sequences. Todd values of virtual classes use inverses, which exist
   because their degree-zero component is one and positive codimension is
   nilpotent.
items.strategy: Apply the splitting principle ([[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]]): after pulling back along the flag bundle $f:X'\to X$ the bundles acquire filtrations with invertible quotients $\mathcal L'_1,\dots$ and $\mathcal L''_1,\dots$, so $\operatorname{ch}(f^*\mathcal E)=\sum_{j}e^{c_1(\mathcal L_j)}$ with the roots running through the union of the roots of $\mathcal E'$ and $\mathcal E''$, giving additivity; injectivity of $f^*$ on the Chow ring concludes (1). Similarly the roots of $\mathcal E$ are those of $\mathcal E'$ together with those of $\mathcal E''$, and $Q(x)=x/(1-e^{-x})$ satisfies $Q(0)=1$, so the products interleave, giving (2). For (3), after splitting both bundles the roots of $\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal F$ are the pairwise sums $x_i+y_j$ and $e^{x_i+y_j}=e^{x_i}e^{y_j}$; duality negates the roots. Statements (4) and (5) are immediate from naturality of Chern classes and the definitions. References: Stacks, *Chow Homology*, Section 42.45 (tag 02UM) for the Chern character as an additive and multiplicative map, Section 42.65 (tag 02UN) for multiplicativity of the Todd class, and Vakil 245 Class 18 Section 2.1 (the two Exercises stated there). The extension to coherent $K_0$ uses the fully proved finite-resolution supplier under its quasi-projective hypothesis. For duality, the degree-$m$ terms of $e^{-x}$ are $(-1)^m$ times those of $e^x$, giving precisely the graded sign formula; no ungraded equality is asserted. All series truncate in codimension above $\dim X$. The exact-sequence roots give an additive map to $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ and a multiplicative map to its units, respectively, hence unique maps on the Grothendieck group (group completion); this supplies the well-definedness on virtual classes.

items.title: Riemann-Roch for projections from projective space
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. Let $k$ be an algebraically
closed field, let $Y$ be a nonsingular equidimensional quasi-projective
$k$-scheme of finite type ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]],
[[cor-smooth-variety-classical-scheme-conventions-agree]]), let $n\ge0$ and let
$$p:\mathbb P^n_k\times_kY\longrightarrow Y$$
be the projection. For every
$\alpha\in K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]):
$$\operatorname{ch}\bigl(p_!(\alpha)\bigr)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\;=\;p_*\Bigl(\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n\times_kY})\Bigr)\qquad\text{in }A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q},$$
where $\operatorname{ch},\operatorname{td}$ are the Chern character and Todd
class of [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]], $p_!$ is the K-theory
pushforward ([[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]],
[[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]) and $p_*$ is the proper
pushforward on Chow groups
([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]). Equivalently, writing
$\tau_X(\alpha)=\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\operatorname{td}(T_X)$, the diagram
$$\begin{array}{ccc}K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY) & \xrightarrow{\ \tau\ } & A^*(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)_{\mathbb Q}\\ \downarrow p_! & & \downarrow p_*\\ K_0(Y) & \xrightarrow{\ \tau\ } & A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}\end{array}$$
commutes. The case $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch for
$\mathbb P^n$, and the case of a general projective-bundle projection is obtained
by the same argument applied to the projective bundle formula.
items.strategy: For smooth quasi-projective $Y$, the K-theory supplier shows $K(\mathbb P^n\times Y)$ is generated by $p_Y^*\beta\otimes p_{\mathbb P}^*\mathcal O(m)$, $0\le m\le n$. Its K pushforward is $\binom{m+n}{n}\beta$, by projective-space cohomology and the K projection formula. Let $h=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$. The Euler exact sequence gives $\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n})=(h/(1-e^{-h}))^{n+1}$ modulo $h^{n+1}$. The Chow integral on the fibre is the coefficient $[h^n]e^{mh}(h/(1-e^{-h}))^{n+1}=\binom{m+n}{n}$. Here is the exact formal residue computation: it equals $\operatorname{Res}_{h=0}e^{mh}(1-e^{-h})^{-n-1}dh$. Substitute $z=1-e^{-h}$, so $dh=dz/(1-z)$ and $e^{mh}=(1-z)^{-m}$; the residue is $[z^n](1-z)^{-m-1}=\binom{m+n}{n}$. Tensor multiplicativity, the tangent product exact sequence and the Chow projection formula now give the desired equality for each generator, hence all classes by additivity. This closes the displayed product-projection theorem. Sources: Borel-Serre1958 §9 Props9-10 and Vakil18-19 (projection portion). For the stated general projective bundle extension, use [[lem-relative-projective-bundle-k-theory-generators]] and the Chow projective bundle basis and the relative Euler sequence; splitting to a flag bundle makes the pushforward coefficient formula the divided difference $\sum_iF(-x_i)/\prod_{j\ne i}(-x_i+x_j)$ in formal roots. The generator integrand $e^{mh}\operatorname{td}(T_{P(E)/Y})$ equals $e^{mh}\prod_j(h+x_j)/(1-e^{-x_j-h})$ in the lines convention. For $m=0,\ldots,r-1$, the divided-difference sum is the character of the appropriate relative symmetric power, by the partial-fraction identity $\prod_j(1-z e^{-x_j})^{-1}=\sum_i\prod_{j\ne i}(1-e^{x_i-x_j})^{-1}(1-z e^{-x_i})^{-1}$. The relative coherent pushforward of these twists is the same symmetric-power bundle (higher direct images vanish); compare using the local monomial basis on trivializations. Both rational functions expand to symmetric polynomials, so equality survives repeated roots; injective flag pullback descends. Apply the base Todd projection formula. The two bundle conventions are exchanged by dualizing $E$, consistently with the displayed quotient convention in the Chow projective bundle supplier.

items.title: Riemann-Roch for a closed embedding of smooth varieties
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. Let $k$ be an algebraically
closed field and $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ a closed immersion of nonsingular
irreducible quasi-projective finite type $k$-varieties, with rank-$d$ normal
bundle $N$. For $E\in K^0(X)=G_0(X)$,
$$\operatorname{ch}(i_*E)=i_*\bigl(\operatorname{ch}(E)\operatorname{td}(N)^{-1}\bigr)\quad\text{in }A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}.$$
Equivalently
$\operatorname{ch}(i_*E)\operatorname{td}(T_Y)=i_*(\operatorname{ch}(E)\operatorname{td}(T_X))$.
The tangent relation is the exact sequence $0\to T_X\to i^*T_Y\to N\to0$, hence
$[i^*T_Y]=[T_X]+[N]$ in $K^0(X)$; a splitting as bundles is neither asserted nor
needed. The two $i_*$ symbols denote respectively coherent $K$ pushforward and
Chow proper pushforward. A vector bundle on $X$ suffices to prove the formula, by
finite resolution and additivity.
items.strategy:
Sources: Vakil19 §2 gives the deformation route but is a sketch in its Koszul step; Borel-Serre1958 §§10-16 independently proves the embedding theorem by the blowup/excess route. The following closes the deformation route locally.
Model case: write $P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(N\oplus1)=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{quot}}(N^\vee\oplus1)$, with projection $p$ and tautological sequence $0\to\mathcal O(-1)\to p^*(N\oplus1)\to Q\to0$. The image of $1$ in $Q$ is a section whose zero scheme is $s:X\hookrightarrow P$, the line $1$; in the last-coordinate-one chart, the quotient basis identifies its actual components with $-z_1,\dots,-z_d$ in $A[z_1,\dots,z_d]$, successively nonzerodivisors after prior coordinates are killed. The tuple is empty for $d=0$; off the distinguished section some component is a unit locally. Thus it meets the rank-d regular-section hypothesis, and $s^*Q=N$. The Koszul resolution of [[lem-koszul-resolution-and-flat-fibre-restriction]], tensored with $p^*E$, gives $\operatorname{ch}(s_*E)=\operatorname{ch}(p^*E)\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{ch}(\bigwedge^jQ^\vee)$, entirely in the ambient ring $A^*(P)_{\mathbb Q}$. After injective flag pullback, if $x_j$ are the roots of $Q$, the sum is $\prod_j(1-e^{-x_j})=c_d(Q)\operatorname{td}(Q)^{-1}$. The regular-section formula gives $c_d(Q)=s_*[X]$ and the ring projection formula gives $c_d(Q)\gamma=s_*(s^*\gamma)$ for every $\gamma\in A^*(P)$. Substituting $\gamma=\operatorname{td}(Q)^{-1}\operatorname{ch}(p^*E)$ proves $\operatorname{ch}(s_*E)=s_*(\operatorname{td}(N)^{-1}\operatorname{ch}(E))$. This corrects the wrongly typed $\operatorname{ch}(i^*E)$ ambient factor.
General case: take $M=\operatorname{Bl}_{X\times\{\infty\}}(Y\times\mathbb P^1)$, its proper projection $b:M\to Y$, and $F:X\times\mathbb P^1\hookrightarrow M$. Resolve $H=F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$ by a bounded complex $G_\bullet$ of vector bundles. Write $\gamma=\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{ch}(G_j)$, an operational class on $M$. The previous helper proves that on $j_0:Y\hookrightarrow M$, $G_\bullet$ resolves $i_*E$; on $k:P\hookrightarrow M$ it resolves $s_*E$; on $l:B\hookrightarrow M$ it is exact. The Cartier fibres at $0,\infty$ are linearly equivalent, hence $j_{0*}[Y]=k_*[P]+l_*[B]$ in $A_*(M)$, with multiplicity one since the centre is smooth. Capping with $\gamma$ and using the Chern projection formula gives
$ j_{0*}(\operatorname{ch}(i_*E)\cap[Y])=k_*(\operatorname{ch}(s_*E)\cap[P]) $;
the $B$ term is zero because its restricted complex is exact. Crucially push this equality by the proper $b$: $bj_0=1_Y$ and $bk=ip$, so $\operatorname{ch}(i_*E)\cap[Y]=i_*p_*(\operatorname{ch}(s_*E)\cap[P])=i_*(\operatorname{ch}(E)\operatorname{td}(N)^{-1}\cap[X])$. The final equality uses the model formula and $ps=1_X$. Thus no injectivity of $j_{0*}$ or informal equality of two fibre rings is assumed. Finite locally free resolution extends from vector bundles to all $K$ classes. Finally Whitney multiplicativity for the tangent exact sequence and the Chow projection formula give the equivalent Todd-tangent formula. Every use of deformation exactness and every pushforward is explicitly typed. The last equality is first an equality in dimension-graded Chow homology; the smooth-ring identification on Y translates it into the displayed codimension-graded ring formula.

items.title: Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch for projective morphisms
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. Let $k$ be an algebraically
closed field and let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of nonsingular
irreducible quasi-projective $k$-schemes of finite type
([[def-projective-morphism-pre-proj]], [[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]],
[[def-proper-morphism]]); projectivity is exactly the hypothesis that $f$ factors
as a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^n_k\times_kY$ followed by the
projection $p:\mathbb P^n_k\times_kY\to Y$ for some $n\ge0$
([[lem-projective-morphism-relative-proj-presentation]]). Then for every
$\alpha\in K_0(X)$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]],
[[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]):
$$\operatorname{ch}\bigl(f_!(\alpha)\bigr)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\;=\;f_*\Bigl(\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_X)\Bigr)\qquad\text{in }A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q},$$
where $\operatorname{ch},\operatorname{td}$ are the Chern character and Todd
class of [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]], $f_!$ is the $K$-theory
pushforward ([[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]]) and $f_*$ is the proper
Chow pushforward ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]).
Equivalently $\tau_Y\circ f_!=f_*\circ\tau_X$ for
$\tau_S(\alpha)=\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\operatorname{td}(T_S)$. For
$Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ this is Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch
$\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\deg(\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)\operatorname{td}(T_X))$
([[def-euler-characteristic-coherent-sheaf]]).
items.strategy: Factor $f=p\circ i$ with $i$ a closed immersion of smooth varieties and $p$ a projection from a projective bundle ([[lem-projective-morphism-relative-proj-presentation]]). Both factors satisfy Riemann-Roch: [[thm-rr-for-regular-embeddings]] for $i$ and [[thm-rr-for-projective-space-projections]] for $p$. The composition step is the elementary diagram chase recorded as Lemma 15(a) of Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 7: the diagram $\tau$ commutes with $i_*$ and with $p_*$, so it commutes with $f_*=p_*i_*$; on the $K$-theory side one uses $(p\circ i)_!=p_!\circ i_!$ ([[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]](2)) and on the Chow side $(p\circ i)_*=p_*i_*$ ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]](2)). Vakil 245 Class 19 states and proves exactly this reduction (``the strategy is now to show GRR for $Y\times\mathbb P^m\to Y$ and for closed immersions'', and the composition Lemma). Borel-Serre 7 states the theorem in the same form for a proper morphism of nonsingular quasi-projective varieties over an algebraically closed field and proves the two special cases in Sections 9 and 15; their Proposition 15 is the injection case and their Corollary in Section 9 is the projection case. Hypotheses: $k$ algebraically closed (Borel-Serre, introduction); $X,Y$ nonsingular irreducible quasi-projective; $f$ projective (hence proper). The statement for arbitrary coherent $\alpha$ follows because $K_0$ is generated by vector bundles ([[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]).

items.title: Conventions, hypotheses and scope of the Chow and Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch development
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. **Conventions.** (i) Rational equivalence is the version of [[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]] (Stacks 42.19.1, tag 02RW; Fulton 1.3), with order functions on possibly singular integral closed subschemes supplied by [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]]; the equivalent $\mathbb P^1$-parametrized definition (Fulton 1.6; Stacks 43.8-43.9) is not used but is consistent with it. (ii) $A^*(X)$ always denotes the codimension-graded intersection ring of a smooth equidimensional $k$-scheme ([[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]); on general schemes $A_*(X)$ and operational Chern cap maps are used; ring-valued Chern classes, character and Todd classes are obtained through the operational identification on smooth schemes. (iii) The intersection product is the diagonal Gysin construction (Stacks 42.62, tag 0FC0); the moving-lemma/Serre Tor-formula construction of Stacks Chapter 43 is an independent route to the same product for nonsingular projective varieties over an algebraically closed field and is not needed here.

**Hypotheses of the main theorem.** [[thm-grothendieck-riemann-roch-for-projective-morphisms]] is stated for an algebraically closed base field $k$, nonsingular irreducible quasi-projective $k$-schemes $X,Y$, and a projective (hence proper) morphism $f$; the field hypothesis agrees with the Borel-Serre proof scope. Vakil Classes 14/16/17/19 are partial comparisons with omitted details; the proposed complete proof is the current local supplier chain, with Borel-Serre introduction and §§7-16 as the independently retrieved comparison. The design-named Fulton source decision remains root-owner-held. No claim is made here for singular targets, for proper non-projective morphisms, for pairs over a non-algebraically-closed field, or in the $K$-theory of perfect complexes; the singular and bivariant versions (Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, Chapters 18 and 17) are outside this pair.

**Choice.** The Axiom of Choice (and, where the coherence of higher direct images is invoked, Dependent Choice) is inherited from the published coherent-cohomology suppliers throughout; it is used to form the resolutions and direct images in [[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]] and is recorded in [[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]. No choice-free claim is made stronger here. The definitional part of the Chow groups uses no choice beyond the free abelian group on a set.
items.strategy: Assembly of conventions, each clause tied to the item that establishes it: (i) rational equivalence is the order-function definition of def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence, with order functions on possibly singular integral subschemes supplied by lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain; (ii) $A^*(X)$ denotes the codimension-graded intersection ring of a smooth equidimensional $k$-scheme (thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme), while for general schemes $A_*(X)$ and operational Chern cap actions are used; (iii) in K-theory, $K_0$ and $K^0$ are identified on regular quasi-projective finite-type schemes (def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme, lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves) and pushforward is defined via higher direct images with the AC/DC inheritance declared (def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory); (iv) the GRR statement proved on this page holds over an algebraically closed field for nonsingular irreducible quasi-projective varieties and projective morphisms (thm-grothendieck-riemann-roch-for-projective-morphisms), and the excluded cases (singular target, arbitrary field, non-projective proper morphisms, perfect-complex formulations, proper-intersection Tor formula) are listed with reasons. No new mathematics is asserted.

items.title: Scheme-theoretic preimages do not define a pullback on Chow groups
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
smooth-immersion and homological suppliers. **Statement refuted.** For every
morphism $f:Y\to X$ of smooth projective $k$-varieties, the **scheme-theoretic
preimage recipe** — send an integral closed subscheme $V\subseteq X$ to the
cycle $[f^{-1}(V)]$ of its scheme-theoretic preimage
([[lem-cycle-of-a-closed-subscheme]]) and extend the assignment linearly to all
cycles — descends to a well-defined homomorphism of abelian groups
$A_*(X)\to A_*(Y)$; that is, preimage cycles of rationally equivalent cycles are
rationally equivalent.
items.strategy: Direct proof in four steps, all from scaffolded and published items. (1) Rational equivalence: $A_0(\mathbb P^2_k)\cong\mathbb Z$ is detected by degree (lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space), so the two $k$-rational points satisfy $[p]=[q]$; equivalently $[p]-[q]=\operatorname{div}(r)$ for the ratio $r$ of linear forms cutting the joining line. (2) Preimage cycles: $\pi^{-1}(p)=E\cong\mathbb P^1$ (thm-blowup-regular-surface-closed-point-regular, def-exceptional-divisor-blowup) and $\pi^{-1}(q)$ is the single reduced point $q'$ over $q\ne p$ (lem-blowup-isomorphism-off-center); the cycle of a preimage scheme is the corresponding basis class (lem-cycle-of-a-closed-subscheme). (3) Suppose the recipe were well defined on rational equivalence; then $[E]=[q']$ in $A_*(Y)$. The proper pushforward of lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined is well defined on rational equivalence and gives $\pi_*[E]=0$ (dimension drop $0<1$) and $\pi_*[q']=[q]$ (isomorphism over $q$, extension degree $1$), hence $[q]=0$, contradicting $\deg[q]=1$. (4) The hypotheses are sharp: pure fibre dimension fails exactly at $p$, so the flat case lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups does not apply, and the correct replacement is the refined Gysin construction of def-refined-gysin-pullback-for-regular-embeddings. State the AC inheritance from the blowup and Proj suppliers.

items.title: The Chow ring of projective space
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the
smooth-immersion and homological suppliers. Let $k$ be a field and $n\ge0$. In
the Chow ring $A^*(\mathbb P^n_k)$
([[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]],
[[lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space]]) put
$h:=c_1(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n}(1))\in A^1(\mathbb P^n)$
([[def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class]],
[[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]). Then:

1. $A^d(\mathbb P^n_k)=\mathbb Z\cdot h^d$ for $0\le d\le n$ and
   $A^d(\mathbb P^n_k)=0$ for $d>n$; under the identification
   $A^d(X)=A_{n-d}(X)$ of the intersection product with the cycle groups, the
   class $h^d$ corresponds to the class $[\Lambda^{n-d}]$ of a linear subspace
   of codimension $d$: equivalently
   $h^d\cap[\mathbb P^n]=[\Lambda^{n-d}]$. In particular
   $$A^*(\mathbb P^n_k)\;\cong\;\mathbb Z[h]/(h^{n+1}),$$
   the isomorphism sending $h$ to $c_1(\mathcal O(1))$.
2. (Degrees of products) The degree isomorphism
   $\deg:A^n(\mathbb P^n_k)\to\mathbb Z$ of
   [[lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space]] satisfies $\deg(h^n)=1$. If
   $H_1,\dots,H_n\subseteq\mathbb P^n$ are reduced hypersurfaces of degrees
   $d_1,\dots,d_n$ ([[def-degree-projective-hypersurface]]) with $H_i=V(f_i)$
   for nonconstant square-free forms $f_i$ of degree $d_i$, then
   $[H_i]=d_i\,h$ in $A^1(\mathbb P^n)$ and
   $$[H_1]\cdot[H_2]\cdots[H_n]=(d_1d_2\cdots d_n)\,h^n,\qquad \deg\bigl([H_1]\cdots[H_n]\bigr)=d_1d_2\cdots d_n.$$

**Discussion.** This is the Chow-ring form of Bezout's theorem: the degree of
the product of the hypersurface classes is the Bezout number. The identification
of this product class with the cycle of the scheme-theoretic intersection of the
$H_i$, with its local intersection multiplicities, is the classical
proper-intersection theorem and is not claimed here; for plane curves ($n=2$,
curves without common components) the corresponding local-multiplicity statement
is developed on the plane-curves page.
items.strategy: Compute, in order: (1) apply the projective bundle formula (thm-projective-bundle-formula-for-chow-groups) to the rank-$(n+1)$ free bundle on $\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose projectivization is $\mathbb P^n_k$, to get $A^*(\mathbb P^n_k)=\mathbb Z[\xi]/(\xi^{n+1})$ with $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; set $h:=\xi$. (2) Identify the generators with linear subspaces: by induction on $d$, intersecting with a hyperplane $H\not\supseteq\Lambda$ of complementary position, the cap-action formula $c_1(\mathcal O(1))\cap[V]=[V\cap H]$ of def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class gives $h^d\cap[\mathbb P^n]=[\Lambda^{n-d}]$, so $A^d(\mathbb P^n)=\mathbb Z\cdot h^d$ corresponds to $A_{n-d}$; in particular $h^n=[\mathrm{pt}]$ with $\deg h^n=1$ (lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space fixes the degree isomorphism on $A_0$). (3) For hypersurfaces $H_i$ of degrees $d_i$, the class is $[H_i]=d_i h$ (def-degree-projective-hypersurface with the normalisation and additivity of $c_1$ from def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle and lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting), so $\deg([H_1]\cdots[H_n])=d_1\cdots d_n$. (4) State explicitly that this computes the product in the Chow ring; the identification with the cycle of the scheme-theoretic intersection is the proper-intersection/Tor-multiplicity statement, deliberately outside this page's scope.
